meta.description: This program accepts and processes updates to credit card account and customer information entered by bank staff through an online screen.
meta.process_description: COACTUPC is an interactive CICS online program that allows bank operations staff to modify existing credit card account details and associated customer profile data. The program presents a data entry screen pre-populated with current account information, validates all user-entered changes against a comprehensive set of business rules, and if valid, persists the updates to the account and customer records. It handles dual-entity updates — both the financial account attributes (credit limits, balances, status, dates) and the customer demographic attributes (name, address, SSN, date of birth, FICO score) — in a single transaction.

business_rules: Account status must be explicitly Y (active) or N (inactive) — no other values permitted
Credit limit, cash credit limit, current balance, cycle credits, and cycle debits must be valid signed numeric amounts
Customer date of birth must be a valid calendar date with year, month, and day each independently validated
Card expiry date and reissue date must be valid calendar dates with all three components (year, month, day) validated
Account open date must be a valid calendar date
US Social Security Number is validated in three segments: Part 1 (3 digits) cannot be 000, 666, or 900-999; Part 2 (2 digits) and Part 3 (4 digits) must be numeric and non-zero
US phone number must conform to standard format (area code + exchange + number) with each segment independently validated as numeric
Customer name fields (first, middle, last) must contain alphabetic characters only
Address fields (line 1, line 2, city, state, zip code, country) must contain alphanumeric characters and are individually validated
The program detects whether any data has actually changed before writing to the database — a no-change submission is identified and handled separately
All mandatory fields must be populated — blank mandatory fields are flagged as a distinct error condition separate from invalid-format errors
The update covers two linked entities simultaneously: the financial account record and the customer demographic record, both must pass validation before any write occurs

variables.name: WS-MISC-STORAGE
variables.description: Top-level working storage container grouping all miscellaneous operational variables used during account update processing, including CICS communication variables and field validation scratch areas.

variables.name: WS-CICS-PROCESSNG-VARS
variables.description: Group of variables used to communicate with the CICS transaction processing environment — captures system responses when reading or writing account and customer records, and identifies the current transaction being executed.

variables.name: WS-RESP-CD
variables.description: CICS response code returned after every file read or write operation (e.g. reading the account master record or writing updated customer data). A non-zero value signals that the database operation failed, triggering error handling to prevent corrupt or partial updates to the account or customer record.

variables.name: WS-REAS-CD
variables.description: CICS reason code that supplements the response code to provide more specific detail about why a file I/O operation failed — for example, distinguishing between a record-not-found condition versus a file unavailable condition when retrieving account or customer records.

variables.name: WS-TRANID
variables.description: The four-character CICS transaction identifier for the account update program. This identifies which transaction the bank operator is currently executing, used for routing and audit purposes within the CardDemo system.

variables.name: WS-UCTRANS
variables.description: Uppercase version of the transaction identifier. Used to normalize the transaction ID to uppercase before comparison or display, ensuring consistent identification of the account update transaction regardless of how the operator entered it.

variables.name: WS-GENERIC-EDITS
variables.description: Group of reusable scratch-pad variables used during field-by-field validation of account and customer data entered on the update screen. These variables are loaded with each field's value in turn and then inspected by shared validation routines before the update is committed.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-VARIABLE-NAME
variables.description: Holds the human-readable name of the field currently being validated (e.g. 'CREDIT LIMIT' or 'DATE OF BIRTH'). Used to construct meaningful error messages that tell the bank operator exactly which field on the account update screen contains invalid data.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-SIGNED-NUMBER-9V2-X
variables.description: Scratch area holding the raw text representation of a monetary amount entered by the bank operator (such as credit limit, cash credit limit, current balance, or cycle credits/debits) before it is validated as a properly signed numeric dollar-and-cents value.

variables.name: WS-FLG-SIGNED-NUMBER-EDIT
variables.description: Validation result flag for a monetary amount field (credit limit, balance, cycle amounts, etc.). Indicates whether the value entered by the bank operator is a valid signed numeric amount, is invalid, or was left blank — controlling whether the update is allowed to proceed.

variables.name: FLG-SIGNED-NUMBER-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that the monetary amount entered (e.g. credit limit or current balance) has passed numeric format validation and is acceptable for saving to the account master record.

variables.name: FLG-SIGNED-NUMBER-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the monetary amount entered by the bank operator is not a valid signed numeric value — for example, contains letters or an invalid sign — and the update must be rejected with an error message.

variables.name: FLG-SIGNED-NUMBER-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating that a required monetary amount field (such as credit limit or current balance) was left blank by the bank operator, triggering a mandatory-field error distinct from a format error.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-ALPHANUM-ONLY
variables.description: Scratch buffer holding the text value of an address or other alphanumeric field entered by the bank operator (street address, city, state, zip, country) while it is being checked to ensure it contains only valid alphanumeric characters before being saved to the customer record.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-ALPHANUM-LENGTH
variables.description: The length of the alphanumeric field currently being validated. Used by the shared validation routine to know how many characters of the address or other text field to inspect, since different fields (street line 1, city, zip, etc.) have different maximum lengths.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-ALPHA-ONLY-FLAGS
variables.description: Validation result flag for fields that must contain alphabetic characters only, such as customer first name, middle name, and last name. Indicates whether the name entered by the bank operator is valid, invalid, or blank.

variables.name: FLG-ALPHA-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that a customer name field (first, middle, or last name) contains only alphabetic characters and has passed validation, allowing the update to proceed.

variables.name: FLG-ALPHA-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that a customer name field contains non-alphabetic characters (such as digits or special characters), which violates the business rule that names must be alphabetic only — the update will be rejected.

variables.name: FLG-ALPHA-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating that a required customer name field was left blank by the bank operator, triggering a mandatory-field error so the operator knows which name field must be filled in.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-ALPHANUM-ONLY-FLAGS
variables.description: Validation result flag for fields that must contain alphanumeric characters only, such as address lines, city, state, zip code, and country. Indicates whether the value entered by the bank operator is valid, invalid, or blank.

variables.name: FLG-ALPHNANUM-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that a customer address field contains only valid alphanumeric characters and has passed validation, allowing the customer record update to proceed.

variables.name: FLG-ALPHNANUM-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that a customer address field contains invalid characters (e.g. special characters not permitted in an address), causing the update to be rejected with an appropriate error message.

variables.name: FLG-ALPHNANUM-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating that a required customer address field was left blank by the bank operator, triggering a mandatory-field error distinct from a format validation error.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-MANDATORY-FLAGS
variables.description: General-purpose mandatory field validation flag used to enforce that required fields on the account update screen have been filled in by the bank operator before the update is allowed to proceed.

variables.name: FLG-MANDATORY-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that a mandatory field has been populated by the bank operator and satisfies the presence requirement, allowing validation to continue to format checks.

variables.name: FLG-MANDATORY-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that a mandatory field on the account update screen has been provided but contains an invalid value, requiring the bank operator to correct it before the update can be saved.

variables.name: FLG-MANDATORY-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating that a mandatory field was left completely blank by the bank operator — a distinct error from an invalid value — prompting the operator to supply the missing required information.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-YES-NO
variables.description: Scratch field holding the value entered by the bank operator for a Yes/No field, most critically the account active/inactive status flag. Used to validate that only 'Y' (active) or 'N' (inactive) has been entered, as required by business rules.

variables.name: FLG-YES-NO-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that the account status field contains a valid value — either 'Y' for active or 'N' for inactive — satisfying the business rule that no other values are permitted for account status.

variables.name: FLG-YES-NO-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the account status field contains an invalid value (neither 'Y' nor 'N'), causing the update to be rejected and the bank operator to be prompted to enter a valid status.

variables.name: FLG-YES-NO-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the account status field was left blank by the bank operator, triggering a mandatory-field error since account status is required and must be explicitly set to active or inactive.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-US-PHONE-NUM
variables.description: The customer's US telephone number as entered by the bank operator on the update screen, stored as a 15-character string in the format NXX-NXX-XXXX before being broken into its three segments (area code, exchange, subscriber number) for individual validation.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-US-PHONE-NUM-X
variables.description: Overlay structure that maps the customer's phone number string into its individual components (area code, exchange, subscriber number) and their separating dashes, enabling each segment to be validated independently against US phone number format rules.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Positional placeholder representing the opening parenthesis or leading separator character in the formatted US phone number string — not used in business logic but required to correctly align the area code segment for extraction.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-US-PHONE-NUMA
variables.description: The three-digit area code portion of the customer's US phone number, extracted from the full phone number string for individual validation against the list of valid North American Numbering Plan area codes.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-US-PHONE-NUMA-N
variables.description: Numeric overlay of the phone area code field, allowing the three-digit area code to be tested as a numeric value to confirm it contains only digits as required by US phone number format rules.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Positional placeholder representing the dash separator between the area code and exchange segments of the US phone number — skipped during validation but required to correctly position the exchange digits.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-US-PHONE-NUMB
variables.description: The three-digit telephone exchange (central office code) portion of the customer's US phone number, extracted for individual validation to ensure it is numeric and conforms to US phone number format requirements.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-US-PHONE-NUMB-N
variables.description: Numeric overlay of the phone exchange field, allowing the three-digit exchange segment to be tested as a numeric value to confirm it contains only digits as part of US phone number format validation.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Positional placeholder representing the dash separator between the exchange and subscriber number segments of the US phone number — skipped during validation but required to correctly position the final four digits.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-US-PHONE-NUMC
variables.description: The four-digit subscriber number (line number) portion of the customer's US phone number, extracted for individual validation to ensure it is numeric and completes a valid US phone number format.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-US-PHONE-NUMC-N
variables.description: Numeric overlay of the phone subscriber number field, allowing the four-digit subscriber segment to be tested as a numeric value to confirm it contains only digits as part of US phone number format validation.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Trailing positional placeholder at the end of the phone number overlay structure, accounting for any remaining characters in the 15-character phone number field beyond the formatted number itself (e.g. closing parenthesis or trailing spaces).

variables.name: WS-EDIT-US-PHONE-NUM-FLGS
variables.description: Composite validation result for the customer's US phone number, combining the individual validation outcomes for the area code, exchange, and subscriber number segments. The overall flag determines whether the phone number entered by the bank operator is acceptable for saving to the customer record.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-US-PHONE-IS-INVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that all three segments of the customer's phone number (area code, exchange, and subscriber number) have failed validation — the entire phone number is invalid and the bank operator must correct it before the customer record can be updated.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-US-PHONE-IS-VALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that all three segments of the customer's US phone number have passed validation — the phone number is correctly formatted and can be saved to the customer master record.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-US-PHONEA-FLG
variables.description: Validation result flag specifically for the area code segment of the customer's US phone number. Indicates whether the three-digit area code is a valid North American Numbering Plan area code, is invalid, or was left blank.

variables.name: FLG-EDIT-US-PHONEA-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that the phone number area code entered by the bank operator is a recognized valid North American area code, satisfying the first segment of US phone number validation.

variables.name: FLG-EDIT-US-PHONEA-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the phone number area code entered by the bank operator is not a valid North American area code — the bank operator must correct the area code before the customer record can be updated.

variables.name: FLG-EDIT-US-PHONEA-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the phone number area code segment was left blank by the bank operator, triggering a mandatory-field error for the phone number area code.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-EDIT-US-PHONEB
variables.description: Validation result flag specifically for the exchange (central office code) segment of the customer's US phone number. Indicates whether the three-digit exchange is numeric and valid, is invalid, or was left blank.

variables.name: FLG-EDIT-US-PHONEB-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that the phone number exchange segment entered by the bank operator is numeric and has passed validation, satisfying the second segment of US phone number format requirements.

variables.name: FLG-EDIT-US-PHONEB-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the phone number exchange segment entered by the bank operator is not valid (e.g. contains non-numeric characters), requiring correction before the customer record can be updated.

variables.name: FLG-EDIT-US-PHONEB-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the phone number exchange segment was left blank by the bank operator, triggering a mandatory-field error for the exchange portion of the customer's phone number.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-EDIT-PHONEC
variables.description: Validation result flag specifically for the subscriber number (line number) segment of the customer's US phone number. Indicates whether the four-digit subscriber number is numeric and valid, is invalid, or was left blank.

variables.name: FLG-EDIT-US-PHONEC-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that the four-digit subscriber number segment of the customer's phone number has passed validation, completing the three-part US phone number format check.

variables.name: FLG-EDIT-US-PHONEC-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the four-digit subscriber number segment of the customer's phone number is invalid (e.g. contains non-numeric characters), requiring the bank operator to correct it.

variables.name: FLG-EDIT-US-PHONEC-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the subscriber number segment of the customer's phone number was left blank by the bank operator, triggering a mandatory-field error for the final segment of the phone number.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-US-SSN
variables.description: The customer's US Social Security Number broken into its three standard segments for independent validation. Each segment is validated separately to enforce SSN business rules (e.g. Part 1 cannot be 000, 666, or 900-999) before the customer record is updated.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-US-SSN-PART1
variables.description: The first three digits of the customer's Social Security Number (the area number). Validated to ensure it is numeric and does not contain prohibited values (000, 666, or the 900-999 range) that would indicate an invalid or fictitious SSN, protecting the bank from fraudulent customer records.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-US-SSN-PART1-N
variables.description: Numeric reinterpretation of the first 3-digit segment of the customer's Social Security Number, allowing the program to perform numeric range checks (e.g. rejecting 000, 666, or 900-999) as required by SSN validation rules.

variables.name: INVALID-SSN-PART1
variables.description: Condition flag that signals the first segment of the customer's SSN is invalid — specifically that it contains a prohibited value (such as 000, 666, or a number in the 900-999 range), which would indicate a fictitious or government-reserved SSN that cannot belong to a real customer.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-US-SSN-PART2
variables.description: The middle 2-digit group number segment of the customer's Social Security Number as entered by the bank operator. This segment is validated independently to ensure it is numeric and non-zero before the account update is allowed to proceed.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-US-SSN-PART2-N
variables.description: Numeric reinterpretation of the middle 2-digit segment of the customer's Social Security Number, enabling the program to perform numeric validity checks (non-zero, all digits) on this portion of the SSN.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-US-SSN-PART3
variables.description: The last 4-digit serial number segment of the customer's Social Security Number as entered by the bank operator. This segment is validated independently to confirm it is numeric and non-zero, ensuring the SSN on the customer record is genuine and complete.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-US-SSN-PART3-N
variables.description: Numeric reinterpretation of the last 4-digit segment of the customer's Social Security Number, allowing numeric validation checks (non-zero, all digits) to be applied to this portion of the SSN before the customer record is updated.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-US-SSN-N
variables.description: Numeric reinterpretation of the entire Social Security Number field, providing a combined numeric view of all three SSN segments to support whole-SSN numeric validation checks during the customer record update process.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-US-SSN-FLGS
variables.description: Group of validation status flags for the customer's Social Security Number. Each of the three SSN segments has its own flag, allowing the program to pinpoint exactly which part of the SSN is missing or invalid and display a precise error message to the bank operator.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-US-SSN-IS-INVALID
variables.description: Condition that is true when all three segments of the customer's SSN have failed validation (all flags set to '0'). When this condition is met, the entire SSN is considered invalid and the account update is blocked until the operator corrects the SSN.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-US-SSN-IS-VALID
variables.description: Condition that is true when all three segments of the customer's SSN have passed validation (all flags are clear/LOW-VALUES). This is the green-light condition that allows the SSN portion of the customer update to proceed to the database write.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-US-SSN-PART1-FLGS
variables.description: Validation status flag for the first 3-digit segment of the customer's SSN. It records whether this segment passed validation, was found to be in an invalid format or prohibited range, or was left blank by the operator — enabling targeted error feedback on the update screen.

variables.name: FLG-EDIT-US-SSN-PART1-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating the first 3-digit SSN segment is valid — it is numeric, non-zero, and not a prohibited value (not 000, 666, or 900-999). The update can proceed for this SSN segment.

variables.name: FLG-EDIT-US-SSN-PART1-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating the first 3-digit SSN segment contains an invalid value — either non-numeric or a prohibited SSN prefix (000, 666, 900-999). The operator must correct this segment before the customer record can be updated.

variables.name: FLG-EDIT-US-SSN-PART1-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating the operator left the first SSN segment blank on the update screen. Since SSN is a mandatory customer identity field, a blank entry is treated as a distinct error requiring the operator to supply the missing information.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-US-SSN-PART2-FLGS
variables.description: Validation status flag for the middle 2-digit group segment of the customer's SSN. Tracks whether this segment is valid, invalid, or blank, enabling the program to provide specific error guidance to the bank operator.

variables.name: FLG-EDIT-US-SSN-PART2-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating the middle 2-digit SSN group number is valid — numeric and non-zero. This segment of the SSN has passed its validation check and does not block the customer record update.

variables.name: FLG-EDIT-US-SSN-PART2-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating the middle 2-digit SSN segment is invalid (non-numeric or zero). The operator must correct this value before the customer record update can be saved to the database.

variables.name: FLG-EDIT-US-SSN-PART2-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating the operator left the middle SSN segment blank. As a mandatory identity field, the missing group number must be supplied before the customer record update is accepted.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-US-SSN-PART3-FLGS
variables.description: Validation status flag for the last 4-digit serial segment of the customer's SSN. Records whether this segment is valid, invalid, or blank, supporting precise error messaging on the account update screen.

variables.name: FLG-EDIT-US-SSN-PART3-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating the last 4-digit SSN serial number is valid — numeric and non-zero. This segment has passed validation and does not prevent the customer record from being updated.

variables.name: FLG-EDIT-US-SSN-PART3-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating the last 4-digit SSN segment is invalid (non-numeric or zero). The operator must provide a correct serial number before the customer record update can be committed.

variables.name: FLG-EDIT-US-SSN-PART3-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating the operator left the last SSN segment blank on the screen. The 4-digit serial number is mandatory for customer identity verification and must be entered before the update is accepted.

variables.name: WS-CALCULATION-VARS
variables.description: Group of working variables used for arithmetic calculations during the account update process, such as date validation arithmetic and any numeric range checks performed on financial or date fields.

variables.name: WS-DIV-BY
variables.description: The divisor used in arithmetic calculations during validation — for example, when checking whether a date component (such as a day value) falls within a valid range by performing division or modulo operations.

variables.name: WS-DIVIDEND
variables.description: The value being divided during arithmetic validation calculations — for example, a date component or numeric field value being tested for validity through division.

variables.name: WS-REMAINDER
variables.description: The remainder produced by a division calculation during validation — used, for example, to determine whether a year is a leap year when validating date fields such as date of birth, account open date, or card expiry date.

variables.name: WS-CURR-DATE
variables.description: The current system date and time at the moment the bank operator submits the update. Used as the reference point for date-range validations — for example, ensuring the card expiry date is in the future and the customer's date of birth is in the past.

variables.name: WS-DATACHANGED-FLAG
variables.description: Tracks whether the bank operator has actually modified any field on the account update screen. Prevents unnecessary and potentially disruptive database writes when the operator submits the screen without making any changes.

variables.name: NO-CHANGES-FOUND
variables.description: Condition indicating that the operator submitted the update screen without changing any data. When true, the program skips the database write and informs the operator that no update was necessary.

variables.name: CHANGE-HAS-OCCURRED
variables.description: Condition indicating that at least one field on the account update screen has been modified by the operator. When true, the program proceeds to validate and then write the changes to the account and customer database records.

variables.name: WS-INPUT-FLAG
variables.description: Overall result of all input validation checks on the update screen. Acts as the master gate — only when all individual field validations pass (INPUT-OK) is the program allowed to write the updated account and customer data to the database.

variables.name: INPUT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that all fields on the account update screen have passed validation. This is the green-light condition that authorises the program to save the updated account and customer information to the database.

variables.name: INPUT-ERROR
variables.description: Condition indicating that one or more fields on the account update screen have failed validation. The database update is blocked and the operator is returned to the screen with error messages highlighting the fields that need correction.

variables.name: INPUT-PENDING
variables.description: Condition indicating that input validation has not yet been performed — typically the initial state when the screen is first displayed to the operator before any data has been submitted for validation.

variables.name: WS-RETURN-FLAG
variables.description: Controls whether the program should return control to the calling menu or parent program after completing (or cancelling) the account update. Governs the navigation flow between the update screen and the rest of the CardDemo application.

variables.name: WS-RETURN-FLAG-OFF
variables.description: Condition indicating the program should remain on the account update screen — the operator has not yet completed or cancelled the update, so control stays within this program.

variables.name: WS-RETURN-FLAG-ON
variables.description: Condition indicating the program should transfer control back to the calling menu or parent program — typically set after a successful update, a cancellation by the operator, or a fatal error that cannot be resolved on this screen.

variables.name: WS-PFK-FLAG
variables.description: Records whether the bank operator pressed a recognised and permitted function key (such as Enter to submit or PF3 to cancel). Prevents the program from processing the screen when an unsupported key is pressed.

variables.name: PFK-VALID
variables.description: Condition indicating the operator pressed a valid, supported function key. The program will proceed to process the screen input according to the key pressed (e.g. submit update, cancel, return to menu).

variables.name: PFK-INVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating the operator pressed an unrecognised or unsupported function key. The program will display an error message and redisplay the screen without processing any data, prompting the operator to use a valid key.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-ACCT-FLAG
variables.description: Validation result for the account number entered on the update screen. Indicates whether the account number is valid and exists in the system, invalid in format, or was left blank — determining whether the account record can be retrieved and updated.

variables.name: FLG-ACCTFILTER-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating the account number entered by the operator is valid and the corresponding account record was successfully found in the system. The program can proceed to display and update the account details.

variables.name: FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating the account number entered is invalid — either it does not exist in the system or it fails format validation. The operator must supply a correct account number before the update can proceed.

variables.name: FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating the operator left the account number field blank on the update screen. Since the account number is the primary key for retrieving the record to be updated, it is mandatory and must be provided.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-CUST-FLAG
variables.description: Validation result for the customer number entered on the update screen. Indicates whether the customer number is valid and matches a customer record linked to the account, is invalid, or was left blank — controlling whether the customer demographic data can be updated.

variables.name: FLG-CUSTFILTER-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating the customer number entered by the operator is valid and the corresponding customer record was found in the system. The program can proceed to display and update the customer's demographic information.

variables.name: FLG-CUSTFILTER-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating the customer number entered is invalid — either it does not exist or fails format validation. The operator must provide a valid customer number before the customer record update can proceed.

variables.name: FLG-CUSTFILTER-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating the operator left the customer number field blank. The customer number is required to identify which customer record to update alongside the account record, so it must be supplied.

variables.name: WS-NON-KEY-FLAGS
variables.description: Group of validation status flags for all non-key data fields on the account update screen (such as account status, credit limits, balances, dates, and customer details). Each flag records the validation outcome for its respective field, collectively determining whether the update can be saved.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-ACCT-STATUS
variables.description: Validation status flag for the account active/inactive status field. Records whether the operator entered a valid status value (Y for active or N for inactive), an invalid value, or left the field blank — enforcing the business rule that only Y or N are permitted.

variables.name: FLG-ACCT-STATUS-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating the account status field contains a valid value — either Y (account is active and can be used for transactions) or N (account is inactive and blocked from use). The update can proceed for this field.

variables.name: FLG-ACCT-STATUS-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating the account status field contains an invalid value — something other than Y or N. The operator must correct this to either Y (active) or N (inactive) before the account record can be updated.

variables.name: FLG-ACCT-STATUS-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating the operator left the account status field blank. Account status is a mandatory field — the operator must explicitly set the account to active (Y) or inactive (N) before the update is accepted.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-CREDIT-LIMIT
variables.description: Validation status flag for the account's total credit limit field. Records whether the credit limit amount entered by the operator is a valid signed numeric value, is in an invalid format, or was left blank — controlling whether this financial limit can be updated on the account record.

variables.name: FLG-CRED-LIMIT-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating the credit limit amount entered is a valid signed numeric value. The maximum amount the cardholder is permitted to charge to this account has passed validation and can be saved to the account master record.

variables.name: FLG-CRED-LIMIT-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating the credit limit amount entered is invalid — for example, contains non-numeric characters or is in an unacceptable format. The operator must correct the credit limit before the account record can be updated.

variables.name: FLG-CRED-LIMIT-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating the operator left the credit limit field blank. The credit limit is a mandatory financial control field on the account — it must be provided to define the maximum borrowing capacity for the cardholder.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT
variables.description: Validation status flag for the account's cash advance credit limit field. Records whether the cash advance limit entered by the operator is a valid signed numeric value, is invalid, or was left blank — this limit controls the maximum cash the cardholder can withdraw against the account.

variables.name: FLG-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating the cash advance credit limit entered is a valid signed numeric value. The maximum amount the cardholder can withdraw as cash against this account has passed validation and can be saved to the account master record.

variables.name: FLG-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating the cash advance credit limit entered is invalid — for example, non-numeric or incorrectly formatted. The operator must supply a valid cash advance limit before the account record update can be committed to the database.

variables.name: FLG-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT-BLANK
variables.description: Condition flag indicating that the bank staff left the cash advance credit limit field completely empty on the update screen. A blank mandatory field is treated as a distinct error from an invalid value — the operator must supply a cash credit limit before the account update can be saved.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-CURR-BAL
variables.description: Validation status flag for the customer's current outstanding account balance entered on the update screen. Holds one of three states: valid (LOW-VALUES), invalid format ('0'), or left blank ('B'). The update cannot proceed to the database if this flag is not in the valid state, ensuring the account balance on record is always a legitimate signed numeric amount.

variables.name: FLG-CURR-BAL-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that the current outstanding balance entered by the bank operator has passed all format and numeric validation checks and is acceptable for saving to the account master record.

variables.name: FLG-CURR-BAL-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the current outstanding balance entered on screen contains an invalid value — for example, non-numeric characters or an improperly formatted signed amount. The operator will be shown an error and must correct the balance before the account record can be updated.

variables.name: FLG-CURR-BAL-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the bank operator left the current outstanding balance field empty on the update screen. Since a balance is required for a valid account record, this blank condition triggers a specific error message distinct from an invalid-format error.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT
variables.description: Validation status flag for the total credit transactions posted to the account during the current billing cycle. Ensures that payments, refunds, and other credits entered by the operator are a valid signed numeric amount before being written to the account master record.

variables.name: FLG-CURR-CYC-CREDIT-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that the current billing cycle credit amount has passed validation and is ready to be saved to the account record.

variables.name: FLG-CURR-CYC-CREDIT-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the current billing cycle credit amount entered on screen is not a valid numeric value. The operator must correct this field before the account update can be committed.

variables.name: FLG-CURR-CYC-CREDIT-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the bank operator left the current billing cycle credit field blank. This is flagged separately from an invalid value so the operator receives a clear message that the field must be populated.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT
variables.description: Validation status flag for the total debit transactions (purchases, fees, charges) posted to the account during the current billing cycle. Prevents invalid or missing debit cycle amounts from being written to the account master record.

variables.name: FLG-CURR-CYC-DEBIT-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that the current billing cycle debit amount has passed all validation checks and is acceptable for saving to the account record.

variables.name: FLG-CURR-CYC-DEBIT-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the current billing cycle debit amount entered on screen is not a valid numeric value. The account update will be blocked until the operator corrects this field.

variables.name: FLG-CURR-CYC-DEBIT-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the bank operator left the current billing cycle debit field blank on the update screen, triggering a specific 'field required' error message.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-DT-OF-BIRTH-FLGS
variables.description: Composite validation record for the customer's date of birth entered on the update screen. Groups three individual component flags (year, month, day) so the program can validate each part of the birth date independently and report precisely which component is missing or invalid. A valid birth date is required to correctly identify the customer and maintain accurate demographic records.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-DT-OF-BIRTH-INVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that all three components of the customer's date of birth (year, month, and day) have failed validation simultaneously. When this fires, the entire birth date is rejected and the operator must re-enter a valid calendar date.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-DT-OF-BIRTH-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that the customer's complete date of birth — year, month, and day — has passed all validation checks and is a legitimate calendar date acceptable for saving to the customer master record.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-DT-OF-BIRTH-YEAR-FLG
variables.description: Validation status flag specifically for the year component of the customer's date of birth. Ensures the birth year entered is a valid numeric value and falls within an acceptable range (i.e., represents a plausible birth year for a living customer).

variables.name: FLG-DT-OF-BIRTH-YEAR-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that the year portion of the customer's date of birth is a valid numeric year and has passed all range checks.

variables.name: FLG-DT-OF-BIRTH-YEAR-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the year portion of the customer's date of birth is not a valid numeric value or falls outside an acceptable range. The operator must correct the birth year before the customer record can be updated.

variables.name: FLG-DT-OF-BIRTH-YEAR-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the bank operator left the birth year field empty. A missing birth year is flagged distinctly so the operator receives a clear 'field required' message rather than a generic format error.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-DT-OF-BIRTH-MONTH
variables.description: Validation status flag specifically for the month component of the customer's date of birth. Ensures the entered month is numeric and falls between 01 and 12, representing a real calendar month.

variables.name: FLG-DT-OF-BIRTH-MONTH-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that the month portion of the customer's date of birth is a valid calendar month (01–12) and has passed all validation checks.

variables.name: FLG-DT-OF-BIRTH-MONTH-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the month portion of the customer's date of birth is invalid — for example, a non-numeric value or a month number outside the range 01–12.

variables.name: FLG-DT-OF-BIRTH-MONTH-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the bank operator left the birth month field blank on the update screen, requiring a specific 'field required' error to be displayed.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-DT-OF-BIRTH-DAY
variables.description: Validation status flag specifically for the day component of the customer's date of birth. Ensures the entered day is numeric and valid for the given month and year (e.g., no 31st in April, no 29th of February in a non-leap year).

variables.name: FLG-DT-OF-BIRTH-DAY-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that the day portion of the customer's date of birth is a valid calendar day for the specified month and year.

variables.name: FLG-DT-OF-BIRTH-DAY-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the day portion of the customer's date of birth is invalid — for example, a non-numeric value or a day that does not exist in the specified month.

variables.name: FLG-DT-OF-BIRTH-DAY-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the bank operator left the birth day field blank, triggering a 'field required' error message so the operator knows exactly which part of the date of birth is missing.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-FICO-SCORE-FLGS
variables.description: Validation status flag for the customer's FICO credit score entered on the update screen. The FICO score is a key creditworthiness indicator used in lending decisions; this flag ensures the value entered is a valid numeric score within the accepted range (typically 300–850) before it is saved to the customer master record.

variables.name: FLG-FICO-SCORE-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that the FICO credit score entered by the operator is a valid numeric value within the acceptable range and can be saved to the customer record.

variables.name: FLG-FICO-SCORE-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the FICO credit score entered on screen is not a valid numeric value or falls outside the acceptable score range. The operator must correct the score before the customer record can be updated.

variables.name: FLG-FICO-SCORE-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the bank operator left the FICO score field blank on the update screen. Since the FICO score is required for credit risk assessment, this triggers a specific 'field required' error.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-OPEN-DATE-FLGS
variables.description: Composite validation record for the account opening date entered on the update screen. Groups three individual component flags (year, month, day) so the program can pinpoint exactly which part of the account open date is missing or invalid. The account open date is a key audit and regulatory field that records when the credit card account was established.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-OPEN-DATE-IS-INVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that all three components of the account opening date (year, month, and day) have simultaneously failed validation. The entire open date is rejected and the operator must re-enter a valid calendar date.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-OPEN-YEAR-FLG
variables.description: Validation status flag for the year component of the account opening date. Ensures the year entered is numeric and represents a plausible year for when a credit card account could have been opened.

variables.name: FLG-OPEN-YEAR-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that the year portion of the account opening date is valid and acceptable for saving to the account master record.

variables.name: FLG-OPEN-YEAR-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the year portion of the account opening date is not a valid numeric value or is outside an acceptable range. The operator must correct the open year before the account record can be updated.

variables.name: FLG-OPEN-YEAR-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the bank operator left the account open year field blank, triggering a 'field required' error so the operator knows the year component of the open date must be supplied.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-OPEN-MONTH
variables.description: Validation status flag for the month component of the account opening date. Ensures the entered month is numeric and represents a valid calendar month (01–12).

variables.name: FLG-OPEN-MONTH-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that the month portion of the account opening date is a valid calendar month and has passed all validation checks.

variables.name: FLG-OPEN-MONTH-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the month portion of the account opening date is invalid — for example, a non-numeric value or a month number outside 01–12.

variables.name: FLG-OPEN-MONTH-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the bank operator left the account open month field blank, requiring a specific 'field required' error message to be displayed.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-OPEN-DAY
variables.description: Validation status flag for the day component of the account opening date. Ensures the entered day is numeric and valid for the given month and year combination.

variables.name: FLG-OPEN-DAY-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that the day portion of the account opening date is a valid calendar day for the specified month and year.

variables.name: FLG-OPEN-DAY-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the day portion of the account opening date is invalid — for example, a non-numeric value or a day that does not exist in the specified month.

variables.name: FLG-OPEN-DAY-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the bank operator left the account open day field blank, triggering a 'field required' error so the operator knows exactly which part of the open date is missing.

variables.name: WS-EXPIRY-DATE-FLGS
variables.description: Composite validation record for the credit card expiry date entered on the update screen. Groups three individual component flags (year, month, day) to allow precise identification of which part of the expiry date is missing or invalid. The expiry date determines when the physical card ceases to be valid for transactions and drives card reissuance processes.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-EXPIRY-IS-INVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that all three components of the card expiry date (year, month, and day) have simultaneously failed validation. The entire expiry date is rejected and the operator must re-enter a valid future calendar date.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-EXPIRY-YEAR-FLG
variables.description: Validation status flag for the year component of the credit card expiry date. Ensures the expiry year is numeric and represents a future year, confirming the card has not already expired at the time of the update.

variables.name: FLG-EXPIRY-YEAR-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that the year portion of the card expiry date is valid and represents an acceptable future year for card validity.

variables.name: FLG-EXPIRY-YEAR-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the year portion of the card expiry date is not a valid numeric value or represents an unacceptable year (e.g., already in the past). The operator must correct the expiry year before the card record can be updated.

variables.name: FLG-EXPIRY-YEAR-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the bank operator left the card expiry year field blank. Since an expiry date is mandatory for every credit card, this triggers a specific 'field required' error.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-EXPIRY-MONTH
variables.description: Validation status flag for the month component of the credit card expiry date. Ensures the entered expiry month is numeric and falls within the valid range of 01–12.

variables.name: FLG-EXPIRY-MONTH-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that the month portion of the card expiry date is a valid calendar month and has passed all validation checks.

variables.name: FLG-EXPIRY-MONTH-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the month portion of the card expiry date is invalid — for example, a non-numeric value or a month number outside 01–12. The operator must correct this before the card record can be saved.

variables.name: FLG-EXPIRY-MONTH-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the bank operator left the card expiry month field blank, triggering a 'field required' error message.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-EXPIRY-DAY
variables.description: Validation status flag for the day component of the credit card expiry date. Ensures the entered expiry day is numeric and valid for the given expiry month and year.

variables.name: FLG-EXPIRY-DAY-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that the day portion of the card expiry date is a valid calendar day for the specified expiry month and year.

variables.name: FLG-EXPIRY-DAY-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the day portion of the card expiry date is invalid — for example, a non-numeric value or a day that does not exist in the specified expiry month. The operator must correct this before the card record can be updated.

variables.name: FLG-EXPIRY-DAY-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the bank operator left the card expiry day field blank, triggering a specific 'field required' error so the operator knows exactly which component of the expiry date is missing.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-REISSUE-DATE-FLGS
variables.description: Composite validation result for the card reissue/renewal date entered by the bank operator. Groups together the individual year, month, and day validation outcomes so the program can determine in one check whether the entire reissue date is acceptable before saving the card record.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-REISSUE-DATE-INVALID
variables.description: Condition that is true when all three components of the card reissue date (year, month, and day) have each been individually flagged as invalid. When this fires, the entire reissue date is rejected and the operator must correct all three parts before the card renewal record can be saved.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-REISSUE-YEAR-FLG
variables.description: Validation status flag for the year portion of the card reissue/renewal date. Holds the outcome of checking whether the year entered by the operator is a plausible calendar year for a card renewal event.

variables.name: FLG-REISSUE-YEAR-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating the reissue year passed all validation checks and is an acceptable calendar year for a card renewal. When true, the year portion will not block the update from proceeding.

variables.name: FLG-REISSUE-YEAR-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating the reissue year entered by the operator failed validation — for example, an out-of-range or non-numeric year. The update will be blocked and the operator must correct the year before the card renewal date can be saved.

variables.name: FLG-REISSUE-YEAR-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating the operator left the reissue year field empty on the update screen. This is treated as a distinct error from an invalid value, allowing the program to display a specific 'field is required' message rather than a generic format error.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-REISSUE-MONTH
variables.description: Validation status flag for the month portion of the card reissue/renewal date. Records whether the month entered (01–12) is a valid calendar month for the card renewal event.

variables.name: FLG-REISSUE-MONTH-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating the reissue month passed validation and represents a real calendar month. When true, the month portion will not prevent the card renewal record from being saved.

variables.name: FLG-REISSUE-MONTH-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating the reissue month entered by the operator is invalid — for example, a value outside 01–12 or a non-numeric entry. The update is blocked until the operator provides a valid month.

variables.name: FLG-REISSUE-MONTH-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating the operator left the reissue month field blank on the screen. Treated separately from an invalid value so the program can prompt the operator specifically that the month is missing.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-REISSUE-DAY
variables.description: Validation status flag for the day portion of the card reissue/renewal date. Records whether the day entered is valid for the given month and year of the card renewal.

variables.name: FLG-REISSUE-DAY-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating the reissue day passed validation and is a legitimate calendar day within the specified month. When true, the day portion will not block saving the card renewal record.

variables.name: FLG-REISSUE-DAY-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating the reissue day entered by the operator is invalid — for example, day 31 in a 30-day month, or a non-numeric entry. The update is blocked until a valid day is provided.

variables.name: FLG-REISSUE-DAY-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating the operator left the reissue day field blank. Treated as a distinct missing-field error so the program can tell the operator specifically that the day of the reissue date must be entered.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-NAME-FLAGS
variables.description: Composite validation result group for the customer's full name as entered on the update screen. Groups the individual first, middle, and last name validation flags so the program can assess overall name validity before writing the customer demographic record.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-FIRST-NAME-FLGS
variables.description: Validation status flag for the customer's first name. Records whether the first name entered by the operator contains only alphabetic characters as required by business rules, or whether it is blank or contains invalid characters.

variables.name: FLG-FIRST-NAME-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating the customer's first name passed validation — it contains only alphabetic characters and is not blank. When true, the first name will not prevent the customer record from being updated.

variables.name: FLG-FIRST-NAME-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating the customer's first name contains invalid characters (e.g., digits or special characters). The update is blocked and the operator must correct the first name to contain alphabetic characters only.

variables.name: FLG-FIRST-NAME-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating the operator left the customer first name field empty. Since a customer must have a first name on record, this triggers a mandatory-field error distinct from a format error.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-MIDDLE-NAME-FLGS
variables.description: Validation status flag for the customer's middle name. Records whether the middle name entered contains only alphabetic characters, is blank, or contains invalid characters.

variables.name: FLG-MIDDLE-NAME-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating the customer's middle name passed validation. When true, the middle name field will not block the customer record update from proceeding.

variables.name: FLG-MIDDLE-NAME-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating the customer's middle name contains invalid characters such as digits or punctuation. The operator must correct the middle name before the customer record can be saved.

variables.name: FLG-MIDDLE-NAME-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating the customer's middle name field was left blank by the operator. Depending on whether middle name is mandatory, this may trigger a required-field warning or be treated as an acceptable omission.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-LAST-NAME-FLGS
variables.description: Validation status flag for the customer's last name (surname). Records whether the last name entered by the operator is alphabetic, blank, or contains invalid characters.

variables.name: FLG-LAST-NAME-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating the customer's last name passed validation and contains only alphabetic characters. When true, the last name will not prevent the customer demographic record from being updated.

variables.name: FLG-LAST-NAME-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating the customer's last name contains invalid characters. The update is blocked and the operator must supply a properly formatted surname before the record can be saved.

variables.name: FLG-LAST-NAME-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating the operator left the customer last name field empty. A customer's surname is a mandatory identifier, so this triggers a required-field error that must be resolved before the update can proceed.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-ADDRESS-FLAGS
variables.description: Composite validation result group for all components of the customer's mailing address entered on the update screen. Groups street lines, city, state, zip code, country, and phone number flags so the program can assess the overall validity of the customer's contact address before writing the customer record.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-ADDRESS-LINE-1-FLGS
variables.description: Validation status flag for the first line of the customer's street address (e.g., house number and street name). Records whether the value entered is alphanumeric, blank, or contains disallowed characters.

variables.name: FLG-ADDRESS-LINE-1-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating the first address line passed validation and contains acceptable alphanumeric content. When true, this field will not block the customer address update.

variables.name: FLG-ADDRESS-LINE-1-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating the first address line contains invalid characters. The operator must correct the street address entry before the customer record can be saved.

variables.name: FLG-ADDRESS-LINE-1-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating the operator left the first address line blank. Since a primary street address is required for the customer record, this triggers a mandatory-field error.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-ADDRESS-LINE-2-FLGS
variables.description: Validation status flag for the second line of the customer's street address (e.g., apartment, suite, or unit number). Records whether the optional secondary address line is valid, blank, or contains disallowed characters.

variables.name: FLG-ADDRESS-LINE-2-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating the second address line passed validation. When true, this field will not prevent the customer address from being updated.

variables.name: FLG-ADDRESS-LINE-2-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating the second address line contains invalid characters. The operator must correct the entry before the customer record can be saved.

variables.name: FLG-ADDRESS-LINE-2-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating the second address line was left blank by the operator. As this is typically an optional field, a blank value may be acceptable and handled differently from a blank mandatory field.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-CITY-FLGS
variables.description: Validation status flag for the city component of the customer's mailing address. Records whether the city name entered by the operator is valid, blank, or contains disallowed characters.

variables.name: FLG-CITY-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating the city name passed validation. When true, the city field will not block the customer address update from proceeding.

variables.name: FLG-CITY-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating the city name entered contains invalid characters. The operator must supply a valid city name before the customer record can be saved.

variables.name: FLG-CITY-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating the operator left the city field blank. City is a required address component, so this triggers a mandatory-field error that must be resolved before the update proceeds.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-STATE-FLGS
variables.description: Validation status flag for the US state code in the customer's mailing address. Records whether the two-letter state abbreviation entered by the operator is a recognized US state code, blank, or invalid.

variables.name: FLG-STATE-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating the state code passed validation against the recognized list of US state abbreviations. When true, the state field will not prevent the customer address from being updated.

variables.name: FLG-STATE-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating the state code entered is not a valid US state abbreviation. The operator must correct the state before the customer record can be saved.

variables.name: FLG-STATE-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating the operator left the state field blank. State is a required address component for US customers, so this triggers a mandatory-field error.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-ZIPCODE-FLGS
variables.description: Validation status flag for the postal ZIP code in the customer's mailing address. Records whether the ZIP code entered by the operator is numeric and in an acceptable format, blank, or invalid.

variables.name: FLG-ZIPCODE-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating the ZIP code passed validation. When true, the ZIP code field will not block the customer address update.

variables.name: FLG-ZIPCODE-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating the ZIP code entered is invalid — for example, contains non-numeric characters or is in an unrecognized format. The operator must correct the ZIP code before the customer record can be saved.

variables.name: FLG-ZIPCODE-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating the operator left the ZIP code field blank. ZIP code is a required address component, so this triggers a mandatory-field error that must be resolved before the update proceeds.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-COUNTRY-FLGS
variables.description: Validation status flag for the country code in the customer's mailing address. Records whether the country value entered by the operator is a recognized alphanumeric country code, blank, or contains invalid characters.

variables.name: FLG-COUNTRY-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating the country code passed validation. When true, the country field will not prevent the customer address record from being updated.

variables.name: FLG-COUNTRY-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating the country code entered is invalid or unrecognized. The operator must supply a valid country code before the customer record can be saved.

variables.name: FLG-COUNTRY-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating the operator left the country field blank. If country is a required address component, this triggers a mandatory-field error.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-PHONE-NUM-1-FLGS
variables.description: Composite validation result group for the customer's primary US phone number. Groups the individual segment flags (area code and exchange) so the program can determine whether the entire phone number is valid before saving the customer contact record.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-PHONE-NUM-1-IS-INVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that at least one segment of the customer's primary phone number failed validation — meaning the overall phone number is unacceptable. The operator must correct the phone number before the customer record can be saved.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-PHONE-NUM-1A-FLG
variables.description: Validation status flag for the area code segment (first three digits) of the customer's primary US phone number. Records whether the area code is a recognized North American Numbering Plan area code, blank, or invalid.

variables.name: FLG-PHONE-NUM-1A-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating the phone area code passed validation against the list of recognized North American area codes. When true, the area code segment will not block the customer record update.

variables.name: FLG-PHONE-NUM-1A-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating the phone area code entered is not a valid North American area code. The operator must correct the area code before the customer contact information can be saved.

variables.name: FLG-PHONE-NUM-1A-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating the operator left the phone area code segment blank. Since a complete phone number is required, this triggers a mandatory-field error for the area code portion.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-PHONE-NUM-1B
variables.description: Validation status flag for the exchange segment (middle three digits, NXX) of the customer's primary US phone number. Records whether this segment is numeric and conforms to the expected phone number format.

variables.name: FLG-PHONE-NUM-1B-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating the phone exchange segment passed validation and is a properly formatted numeric value. When true, this segment will not prevent the customer phone number from being accepted.

variables.name: FLG-PHONE-NUM-1B-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating the phone exchange segment entered is invalid — for example, contains non-numeric characters. The operator must correct this portion of the phone number before the customer record can be saved.

variables.name: FLG-PHONE-NUM-1B-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating the operator left the phone exchange segment blank. Since a complete phone number requires all segments, this triggers a mandatory-field error for the exchange portion of the primary phone number.

variables.name: FLG-PHONE-NUM-1B-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition flag indicating that the second digit segment of the customer's phone area code failed validation — the bank operator must correct this portion before the update can be saved.

variables.name: FLG-PHONE-NUM-1B-BLANK
variables.description: Condition flag indicating that the second digit segment of the customer's phone area code was left blank by the operator — used to distinguish a missing entry from an incorrectly formatted one.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-PHONE-NUM-1C
variables.description: Validation status flag for the third digit segment of the customer's US phone area code. Tracks whether this portion of the area code passed, failed, or was left blank during the update screen validation process.

variables.name: FLG-PHONE-NUM-1C-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition flag confirming that the third digit segment of the customer's phone area code has passed validation and is acceptable for saving to the customer record.

variables.name: FLG-PHONE-NUM-1C-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition flag indicating that the third digit segment of the customer's phone area code failed validation — the bank operator must correct this portion before the update can proceed.

variables.name: FLG-PHONE-NUM-1C-BLANK
variables.description: Condition flag indicating that the third digit segment of the customer's phone area code was left blank — distinguishes a missing entry from an incorrectly formatted one so the operator receives the appropriate error message.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-PHONE-NUM-2-FLGS
variables.description: Group of validation status flags covering all three digit segments of the customer's US phone exchange (central office code — the middle three digits of the phone number). All segments must pass for the phone number to be accepted.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-PHONE-NUM-2-IS-INVALID
variables.description: Composite condition flag that signals the entire phone exchange segment (middle three digits of the customer's US phone number) is invalid — used to block the account update and prompt the operator to correct the phone number.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-PHONE-NUM-2A-FLG
variables.description: Validation status flag for the first digit of the customer's US phone exchange segment. Tracks whether this digit passed, failed, or was left blank during screen input validation.

variables.name: FLG-PHONE-NUM-2A-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition flag confirming that the first digit of the customer's phone exchange segment has passed validation and is acceptable for saving to the customer record.

variables.name: FLG-PHONE-NUM-2A-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition flag indicating that the first digit of the customer's phone exchange segment failed validation — the operator must correct this before the update can be saved.

variables.name: FLG-PHONE-NUM-2A-BLANK
variables.description: Condition flag indicating that the first digit of the customer's phone exchange segment was left blank — distinguishes a missing mandatory entry from an incorrectly formatted one.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-PHONE-NUM-2B
variables.description: Validation status flag for the second digit of the customer's US phone exchange segment. Tracks whether this digit passed, failed, or was left blank during screen input validation.

variables.name: FLG-PHONE-NUM-2B-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition flag confirming that the second digit of the customer's phone exchange segment has passed validation and is acceptable for saving to the customer record.

variables.name: FLG-PHONE-NUM-2B-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition flag indicating that the second digit of the customer's phone exchange segment failed validation — the operator must correct this before the update can be saved.

variables.name: FLG-PHONE-NUM-2B-BLANK
variables.description: Condition flag indicating that the second digit of the customer's phone exchange segment was left blank — distinguishes a missing mandatory entry from an incorrectly formatted one.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-PHONE-NUM-2C
variables.description: Validation status flag for the third digit of the customer's US phone exchange segment. Tracks whether this digit passed, failed, or was left blank during screen input validation.

variables.name: FLG-PHONE-NUM-2C-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition flag confirming that the third digit of the customer's phone exchange segment has passed validation and is acceptable for saving to the customer record.

variables.name: FLG-PHONE-NUM-2C-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition flag indicating that the third digit of the customer's phone exchange segment failed validation — the operator must correct this before the update can be saved.

variables.name: FLG-PHONE-NUM-2C-BLANK
variables.description: Condition flag indicating that the third digit of the customer's phone exchange segment was left blank — distinguishes a missing mandatory entry from an incorrectly formatted one.

variables.name: WS-EFT-ACCOUNT-ID-FLGS
variables.description: Validation status flag for the customer's Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) bank account identifier — used when the customer has a linked external bank account for payments or direct debit. Tracks whether the EFT account ID entered on screen is valid, invalid, or blank.

variables.name: FLG-EFT-ACCOUNT-ID-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition flag confirming that the customer's EFT bank account identifier has passed validation and can be saved to the customer record.

variables.name: FLG-EFT-ACCOUNT-ID-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition flag indicating that the customer's EFT bank account identifier failed validation — the operator must correct this value before the update can proceed.

variables.name: FLG-EFT-ACCOUNT-ID-BLANK
variables.description: Condition flag indicating that the customer's EFT bank account identifier was left blank on the update screen — distinguishes a missing entry from an incorrectly formatted one for appropriate error messaging.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-PRI-CARDHOLDER
variables.description: Validation status flag indicating whether the customer being updated is designated as the primary cardholder on the account. Must be explicitly Y (yes, primary) or N (no, supplementary) — any other value or blank is rejected to ensure clear account ownership is recorded.

variables.name: FLG-PRI-CARDHOLDER-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition flag confirming that the primary cardholder designation has been set to a valid value (Y or N) — the account update can proceed with this field as entered.

variables.name: FLG-PRI-CARDHOLDER-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition flag indicating that the primary cardholder designation contains an invalid value — the operator must enter Y or N before the update can be saved.

variables.name: FLG-PRI-CARDHOLDER-BLANK
variables.description: Condition flag indicating that the primary cardholder designation was left blank — this mandatory field must be completed before the account update can proceed.

variables.name: CICS-OUTPUT-EDIT-VARS
variables.description: Group of working variables used to format and validate data before it is displayed on the account update screen or written to the database — acts as a staging area for converting raw input into properly formatted account and customer field values.

variables.name: CUST-ACCT-ID-X
variables.description: The customer's account identifier held as a text string — used when displaying the account number on screen or when the account ID needs to be treated as character data for formatting or comparison purposes.

variables.name: CUST-ACCT-ID-N
variables.description: The customer's account identifier reinterpreted as a numeric value — allows arithmetic operations or numeric comparisons on the same account ID field without duplicating storage, used during validation and database lookup.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-DATE-X
variables.description: A general-purpose date field in display format (YYYY-MM-DD) used as a working area when validating or formatting dates entered on the account update screen — such as account open date, card expiry date, or customer date of birth.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Redefines the general-purpose date field to expose its individual components (year, separator, month, separator, day) so each part can be independently extracted and validated during date checking on the account update screen.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-DATE-X-YEAR
variables.description: The four-digit year portion of a date being validated on the account update screen — used to check that the year component of dates such as account open date, card expiry, or date of birth is within an acceptable range.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: The separator character (typically a hyphen) between the year and month portions of a date displayed on screen — not used for business logic but required to correctly parse the formatted date string.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-DATE-MONTH
variables.description: The two-digit month portion of a date being validated on the account update screen — used to verify that the month component of dates such as account open date, card expiry, or date of birth is a valid calendar month (01–12).

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: The separator character (typically a hyphen) between the month and day portions of a date displayed on screen — not used for business logic but required to correctly parse the formatted date string.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-DATE-DAY
variables.description: The two-digit day portion of a date being validated on the account update screen — used to verify that the day component of dates such as account open date, card expiry, or date of birth is a valid calendar day for the given month and year.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-DATE-X
variables.description: A second redefinition of the general-purpose date working area — allows the same date storage to be accessed in an alternative format or structure during different stages of date validation and formatting on the account update screen.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-CURRENCY-9-2
variables.description: A working area that holds a monetary amount as a character string — used as an intermediate buffer when receiving currency values (such as credit limit, cash limit, or current balance) from the screen before converting them to numeric format for validation and storage.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-CURRENCY-9-2-F
variables.description: A formatted numeric field used to display monetary amounts (such as credit limit, cash advance limit, or current balance) on the account update screen in a human-readable format with sign, comma separators, and two decimal places — ensures bank staff see properly formatted currency values.

variables.name: WS-XREF-RID
variables.description: Cross-reference record identifier group — holds the key fields (card number, customer ID, account ID) needed to look up and link the credit card record, customer record, and account record across the three related database files during the update process.

variables.name: WS-CARD-RID-CARDNUM
