variables.description: The 16-digit credit card number used as the primary key to locate the card record in the credit card file — this is the card number printed on the customer's physical card and is the starting point for retrieving all related account and customer information.

variables.name: WS-CARD-RID-CUST-ID
variables.description: The nine-digit customer identifier used as the key to retrieve the customer's demographic record from the customer master file — links the credit card to the specific customer who holds it.

variables.name: WS-CARD-RID-CUST-ID-X
variables.description: The customer identifier reinterpreted as a character string — allows the numeric customer ID to be used in character-based comparisons, screen display, or file key construction without duplicating storage.

variables.name: WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID
variables.description: The eleven-digit account identifier used as the key to retrieve the financial account record from the account master file — links the credit card to the specific credit account holding the balance, limits, and status information.

variables.name: WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID-X
variables.description: The account identifier reinterpreted as a character string — allows the numeric account ID to be used in character-based comparisons, screen display, or file key construction without duplicating storage.

variables.name: WS-FILE-READ-FLAGS
variables.description: Group of flags that record whether the account master record and customer master record were successfully retrieved from the database — both records must be found before the update screen can be populated or any changes saved.

variables.name: WS-ACCOUNT-MASTER-READ-FLAG
variables.description: Tracks whether the financial account master record was successfully read from the database for the account being updated — if the account cannot be found, the update cannot proceed and the operator is notified.

variables.name: FOUND-ACCT-IN-MASTER
variables.description: Condition flag confirming that the account master record was successfully retrieved from the database — the program can proceed to display and update the account's financial details such as credit limit, balance, and status.

variables.name: WS-CUST-MASTER-READ-FLAG
variables.description: Tracks whether the customer demographic master record was successfully read from the database for the customer linked to the account being updated — if the customer record cannot be found, the update cannot proceed.

variables.name: FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER
variables.description: Condition flag confirming that the customer master record was successfully retrieved from the database — the program can proceed to display and update the customer's personal details such as name, address, date of birth, and SSN.

variables.name: WS-FILE-ERROR-MESSAGE
variables.description: A structured error message displayed to the bank operator when a database file operation (read, write, or update) fails — identifies which operation was attempted, which file was involved, and the system error response code so the operator or support team can diagnose the problem.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Fixed label text at the start of the file error message (e.g. 'ERROR ON  ') — provides a readable prefix so the operator immediately recognises the message as a file access error.

variables.name: ERROR-OPNAME
variables.description: The name of the database operation that failed (e.g. 'READ', 'WRITE', 'REWRITE') — tells the operator and support team exactly what action was being performed on the account or customer record when the error occurred.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Fixed spacing or label text between the operation name and file name in the error message — improves readability of the error displayed to the bank operator.

variables.name: ERROR-FILE
variables.description: The name of the database file that experienced the error (e.g. the account master file or customer master file) — identifies which data store was being accessed when the failure occurred, helping support staff locate and resolve the issue.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Fixed spacing or label text between the file name and the error response code in the error message — improves readability of the error displayed to the bank operator.

variables.name: ERROR-RESP
variables.description: The CICS system response code returned when the database operation failed — provides the technical error code that support staff can use to diagnose the exact nature of the file access failure (e.g. record not found, file unavailable, duplicate key).

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Fixed trailing spacing or label text at the end of the file error message — pads the message to its full display length and may contain additional context text for the operator.

variables.name: ERROR-RESP2
variables.description: Stores the secondary CICS error response code when a file operation (such as reading or writing an account or customer record) fails. Used by bank staff support and developers to diagnose the exact reason a database update could not be completed — for example, why a card account record could not be saved.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Reserved padding space within the error response area. Has no direct business meaning; it ensures proper memory alignment of the surrounding error-handling fields so that error codes are read and written correctly.

variables.name: ALPHA-VARS-FOR-DATA-EDITING
variables.description: A group of temporary text-format holding areas used during input validation. When a bank operator types financial amounts on the update screen, these fields capture the raw text before the program checks whether the values are valid numbers. This prevents the program from crashing on non-numeric input and allows meaningful error messages to be shown to the operator.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CREDIT-LIMIT-X
variables.description: Temporary text representation of the new credit limit amount entered by the bank operator on the account update screen. Held as plain text so the program can validate it is a proper numeric amount before applying it to the customer's account as the maximum total credit they are allowed to carry.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT-X
variables.description: Temporary text representation of the new cash advance credit limit entered by the bank operator. Held as plain text for validation before being applied to the account as the maximum amount the cardholder is permitted to withdraw as a cash advance.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CURR-BAL-X
variables.description: Temporary text representation of the current outstanding balance entered by the bank operator. Held as plain text for validation before being recorded as the cardholder's current amount owed on the account.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CURR-CYC-CREDIT-X
variables.description: Temporary text representation of the total credits posted in the current billing cycle, as entered by the bank operator. Held as plain text for validation before being recorded — this represents payments and credits applied to the account during the current statement period.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CURR-CYC-DEBIT-X
variables.description: Temporary text representation of the total debits posted in the current billing cycle, as entered by the bank operator. Held as plain text for validation before being recorded — this represents purchases and charges made on the account during the current statement period.

variables.name: ACCT-UPDATE-RECORD
variables.description: The complete financial account record being prepared for update. This structure holds all validated account-level data that will be written to the credit card account master file once the bank operator confirms the changes. It represents the core financial profile of a credit card account.

variables.name: ACCT-UPDATE-ID
variables.description: The unique 11-digit account identifier for the credit card account being updated. This is the primary key used to locate and update the correct account record in the account master file — it uniquely identifies one customer's credit card account within the bank's system.

variables.name: ACCT-UPDATE-ACTIVE-STATUS
variables.description: Indicates whether the credit card account is currently active or inactive. Must be set to 'Y' (account is open and usable) or 'N' (account is closed or suspended). Bank operators use this to activate or deactivate a customer's account as part of account management.

variables.name: ACCT-UPDATE-CURR-BAL
variables.description: The current outstanding balance on the credit card account, stored as a signed numeric value with two decimal places. This is the total amount the cardholder currently owes to the bank, and can be negative (representing a credit in the customer's favor).

variables.name: ACCT-UPDATE-CREDIT-LIMIT
variables.description: The maximum total credit limit approved for this credit card account, stored as a signed numeric value with two decimal places. This is the highest balance the cardholder is permitted to carry — purchases that would exceed this limit should be declined.

variables.name: ACCT-UPDATE-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT
variables.description: The maximum amount the cardholder is permitted to withdraw as cash advances on this account, stored as a signed numeric value with two decimal places. This sub-limit is typically lower than the overall credit limit and governs ATM and cash advance transactions.

variables.name: ACCT-UPDATE-OPEN-DATE
variables.description: The date on which the credit card account was originally opened, stored in a 10-character format (YYYY-MM-DD). This is a key piece of account history used for tenure tracking, regulatory reporting, and determining how long the customer has held the account.

variables.name: ACCT-UPDATE-EXPIRAION-DATE
variables.description: The expiration date of the credit card associated with this account, stored in a 10-character format (YYYY-MM-DD). After this date the physical card is no longer valid for transactions, and a new card must be issued to the cardholder.

variables.name: ACCT-UPDATE-REISSUE-DATE
variables.description: The date on which the credit card was most recently reissued or renewed to the cardholder, stored in a 10-character format (YYYY-MM-DD). This tracks when a replacement card was sent, which is important for card lifecycle management and fraud investigation.

variables.name: ACCT-UPDATE-CURR-CYC-CREDIT
variables.description: The total amount of credits (payments, refunds, adjustments) posted to the account during the current billing cycle, stored as a signed numeric value with two decimal places. Used in statement generation and balance calculation for the current period.

variables.name: ACCT-UPDATE-CURR-CYC-DEBIT
variables.description: The total amount of debits (purchases, fees, interest charges) posted to the account during the current billing cycle, stored as a signed numeric value with two decimal places. Used in statement generation and balance calculation for the current period.

variables.name: ACCT-UPDATE-GROUP-ID
variables.description: An identifier linking this credit card account to a specific product group, pricing tier, or customer segment within the bank. This may determine which fee schedules, interest rates, or reward programs apply to the account.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Reserved padding space within the account update record to align the total record length with the physical account master file layout. Has no direct business meaning but ensures the record written to the database matches the expected file structure exactly.

variables.name: CUST-UPDATE-RECORD
variables.description: The complete customer demographic record being prepared for update. This structure holds all validated personal and contact information about the cardholder that will be written to the customer master file once the bank operator confirms the changes. It represents the identity and contact profile of the customer.

variables.name: CUST-UPDATE-ID
variables.description: The unique 9-digit customer identifier for the individual whose demographic information is being updated. This is the primary key used to locate and update the correct customer record in the customer master file — it uniquely identifies one person within the bank's customer database.

variables.name: CUST-UPDATE-FIRST-NAME
variables.description: The customer's legal first (given) name, up to 25 characters. Must contain alphabetic characters only. Used for customer identification, correspondence, and regulatory compliance — ensuring the bank addresses and identifies the cardholder correctly.

variables.name: CUST-UPDATE-MIDDLE-NAME
variables.description: The customer's legal middle name, up to 25 characters. Must contain alphabetic characters only. Used to fully identify the customer, particularly when first and last names alone are insufficient to distinguish between customers with similar names.

variables.name: CUST-UPDATE-LAST-NAME
variables.description: The customer's legal last (family/surname) name, up to 25 characters. Must contain alphabetic characters only. A mandatory identification field used across all customer communications, statements, and regulatory reporting.

variables.name: CUST-UPDATE-ADDR-LINE-1
variables.description: The first line of the customer's mailing address (typically street number and street name), up to 50 characters. Used for sending account statements, card mailings, and other bank correspondence to the cardholder's physical location.

variables.name: CUST-UPDATE-ADDR-LINE-2
variables.description: The second line of the customer's mailing address (typically apartment, suite, or unit number), up to 50 characters. Supplements the primary address line to ensure accurate mail delivery to the cardholder.

variables.name: CUST-UPDATE-ADDR-LINE-3
variables.description: The third line of the customer's mailing address (typically city name), up to 50 characters. Part of the complete address used for delivering statements and correspondence to the cardholder.

variables.name: CUST-UPDATE-ADDR-STATE-CD
variables.description: The two-character US state code for the customer's mailing address (e.g., 'CA' for California, 'NY' for New York). Used to complete the mailing address and may also be used for state-level regulatory reporting and tax purposes.

variables.name: CUST-UPDATE-ADDR-COUNTRY-CD
variables.description: The three-character country code for the customer's mailing address (e.g., 'USA'). Identifies the country of residence for the cardholder, which is relevant for international compliance, sanctions screening, and cross-border regulatory requirements.

variables.name: CUST-UPDATE-ADDR-ZIP
variables.description: The postal ZIP code for the customer's mailing address, up to 10 characters (accommodating both 5-digit and ZIP+4 formats). Used to complete the mailing address and may be used for geographic segmentation and fraud detection.

variables.name: CUST-UPDATE-PHONE-NUM-1
variables.description: The customer's primary contact phone number in US format, up to 15 characters. Used by the bank to contact the cardholder for account alerts, fraud verification, collections, and customer service. Must conform to standard US phone number format validation.

variables.name: CUST-UPDATE-PHONE-NUM-2
variables.description: The customer's secondary or alternate contact phone number in US format, up to 15 characters. Provides a backup contact method for the bank to reach the cardholder when the primary number is unavailable.

variables.name: CUST-UPDATE-SSN
variables.description: The customer's 9-digit US Social Security Number stored as a numeric value. This is a critical government-issued identity identifier used for regulatory compliance (e.g., KYC — Know Your Customer), credit bureau reporting, and uniquely verifying the customer's legal identity.

variables.name: CUST-UPDATE-GOVT-ISSUED-ID
variables.description: An alternative government-issued identification number for the customer (such as a passport number or driver's license number), up to 20 characters. Used as a supplementary identity verification document, particularly for customers who may not have a US Social Security Number.

variables.name: CUST-UPDATE-DOB-YYYY-MM-DD
variables.description: The customer's date of birth in YYYY-MM-DD format. Used for identity verification, age eligibility checks (e.g., confirming the cardholder is of legal age), regulatory compliance, and fraud prevention. Must be a valid past calendar date.

variables.name: CUST-UPDATE-EFT-ACCOUNT-ID
variables.description: The identifier for the customer's linked Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) bank account, up to 10 characters. This links the credit card account to a checking or savings account used for automatic payments, direct debits, or balance transfers.

variables.name: CUST-UPDATE-PRI-CARD-IND
variables.description: A single-character indicator showing whether this customer record is associated with the primary cardholder on the account. Distinguishes the main account holder from authorized secondary cardholders, which affects billing responsibility and account privileges.

variables.name: CUST-UPDATE-FICO-CREDIT-SCORE
variables.description: The customer's FICO credit score, a 3-digit number typically ranging from 300 to 850. This score reflects the customer's creditworthiness and is used by the bank to assess lending risk, determine credit limits, and set interest rates on the account.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Reserved padding space within the customer update record to align the total record length with the physical customer master file layout. Has no direct business meaning but ensures the record written to the database matches the expected file structure exactly.

variables.name: WS-LONG-MSG
variables.description: A large 500-character message area used to hold extended diagnostic or informational text. Used internally to construct detailed error descriptions or processing messages that may be logged or displayed when a complex validation failure or system error occurs during the account update process.

variables.name: WS-INFO-MSG
variables.description: A 40-character field that holds the current instructional or status message displayed to the bank operator on the account update screen. Its value drives what guidance or feedback the operator sees at any given point in the update workflow.

variables.name: WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE
variables.description: Condition indicating that no informational message is currently set for the operator. The screen message area is blank, meaning the program has not yet determined what guidance to show the bank operator.

variables.name: FOUND-ACCOUNT-DATA
variables.description: Condition indicating that the account and customer records were successfully retrieved from the database and are now displayed on screen. The bank operator can see the current account data and is ready to make changes.

variables.name: PROMPT-FOR-SEARCH-KEYS
variables.description: Condition indicating that the screen is prompting the bank operator to enter the account or customer identifier needed to look up the record they wish to update. The operator has not yet provided search criteria.

variables.name: PROMPT-FOR-CHANGES
variables.description: Condition indicating that the account data has been loaded and the screen is now prompting the bank operator to enter the changes they wish to make to the account or customer record.

variables.name: PROMPT-FOR-CONFIRMATION
variables.description: Condition indicating that the operator's changes have passed validation and the screen is now asking the operator to confirm that they want to save the changes to the account and customer records. This is the final check before the database is updated.

variables.name: CONFIRM-UPDATE-SUCCESS
variables.description: Condition indicating that the account and customer records were successfully updated in the database. The screen displays a success confirmation to the bank operator, confirming the changes have been saved.

variables.name: INFORM-FAILURE
variables.description: Condition indicating that the update process failed — either due to a validation error or a database write failure. The screen informs the bank operator that the changes could not be saved and further action is required.

variables.name: WS-RETURN-MSG
variables.description: A 75-character message field used to pass a status or instructional message back to the calling menu program when the operator exits the account update screen. This message may inform the operator or the next screen about the outcome of the update session.

variables.name: WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF
variables.description: Condition indicating that no return message has been set. The operator is not being sent back to the calling program with any specific message — the return message area is blank.

variables.name: WS-EXIT-MESSAGE
variables.description: Condition indicating that the return message is a general exit notification, signalling to the calling program that the operator has chosen to leave the account update screen and return to the menu.

variables.name: WS-PROMPT-FOR-ACCT
variables.description: Condition indicating that the return message is instructing the operator (or the calling program) that an account number must be provided before the update process can begin. No account has been identified yet.

variables.name: WS-PROMPT-FOR-LASTNAME
variables.description: Condition indicating that the return message is instructing the operator that a customer last name must be provided as a search criterion. The program requires this information to locate the correct customer record.

variables.name: WS-NAME-MUST-BE-ALPHA
variables.description: Condition indicating that the return message is informing the operator that a name field they entered contains invalid characters — names must contain alphabetic characters only. The operator must correct the entry before the update can proceed.

variables.name: NO-SEARCH-CRITERIA-RECEIVED
variables.description: Condition indicating that the return message is informing the operator that they submitted the screen without entering any search criteria (account number or customer identifier). The program cannot look up a record without at least one search key.

variables.name: NO-CHANGES-DETECTED
variables.description: Condition indicating that the return message is informing the operator that the data they submitted is identical to what is already stored in the database — no fields were actually changed. The program will not perform an unnecessary database write in this case.

variables.name: SEARCHED-ACCT-ZEROES
variables.description: Condition indicating that the return message is informing the operator that the account number they entered consists entirely of zeros, which is not a valid account number. The operator must enter a real account identifier.

variables.name: SEARCHED-ACCT-NOT-NUMERIC
variables.description: Condition indicating that the return message is informing the operator that the account number they entered contains non-numeric characters. Account numbers must be entirely numeric, and the operator must correct their entry before the search can proceed.

variables.name: DID-NOT-FIND-ACCT-IN-CARDXREF
variables.description: Error condition indicating that the account number entered by the bank operator could not be found in the card cross-reference file (CARDXREF), meaning no credit card is linked to this account. The update cannot proceed because the account-to-card relationship does not exist.

variables.name: DID-NOT-FIND-ACCT-IN-ACCTDAT
variables.description: Error condition indicating that the account number entered by the bank operator does not exist in the account master file (ACCTDAT). The update cannot proceed because there is no financial account record to update.

variables.name: DID-NOT-FIND-CUST-IN-CUSTDAT
variables.description: Error condition indicating that the customer number associated with the account cannot be found in the customer master file (CUSTDAT). The update cannot proceed because there is no customer demographic record to update alongside the account record.

variables.name: ACCT-STATUS-MUST-BE-YES-NO
variables.description: Validation error condition indicating that the account status field entered by the operator contains an invalid value. Per business rules, account status must be exactly 'Y' (active) or 'N' (inactive) — any other entry is rejected.

variables.name: CRED-LIMIT-IS-BLANK
variables.description: Validation error condition indicating that the credit limit field was left empty by the operator. Credit limit is a mandatory field — a blank submission is flagged as a distinct error separate from an invalid format error, preventing the account update from proceeding.

variables.name: CRED-LIMIT-IS-NOT-VALID
variables.description: Validation error condition indicating that the credit limit amount entered by the operator is not a valid signed numeric value. The credit limit must be a properly formatted monetary amount before the account record can be updated.

variables.name: THIS-MONTH-NOT-VALID
variables.description: Validation error condition indicating that a month component of a date field (such as account open date, card expiry date, reissue date, or customer date of birth) entered by the operator is not a valid calendar month (i.e., not between 01 and 12).

variables.name: THIS-YEAR-NOT-VALID
variables.description: Validation error condition indicating that a year component of a date field (such as account open date, card expiry date, reissue date, or customer date of birth) entered by the operator is not a valid calendar year, preventing the account or customer record from being updated.

variables.name: DID-NOT-FIND-ACCT-IN-CARDXREF
variables.description: Duplicate error condition flag (second occurrence) indicating that the account number could not be located in the card cross-reference file during a subsequent lookup step, confirming that no valid card-to-account linkage exists and the update must be aborted.

variables.name: DID-NOT-FIND-ACCTCARD-COMBO
variables.description: Error condition indicating that the specific combination of account number and card number entered by the operator does not exist as a matched pair in the system. Even if each exists individually, the account-card pairing must be valid before any update is permitted.

variables.name: COULD-NOT-LOCK-ACCT-FOR-UPDATE
variables.description: Error condition indicating that the system was unable to obtain an exclusive lock on the account master record for update. This typically means another bank operator or process is currently modifying the same account, and the update must be deferred to prevent data corruption.

variables.name: COULD-NOT-LOCK-CUST-FOR-UPDATE
variables.description: Error condition indicating that the system was unable to obtain an exclusive lock on the customer master record for update. Similar to the account lock failure, this prevents simultaneous conflicting updates to the customer's demographic information by multiple operators.

variables.name: DATA-WAS-CHANGED-BEFORE-UPDATE
variables.description: Error condition indicating that the account or customer data in the database was modified by another process between the time the operator retrieved the record for display and the time they submitted their changes. This protects against overwriting a more recent update with stale data.

variables.name: LOCKED-BUT-UPDATE-FAILED
variables.description: Error condition indicating a critical failure scenario where the system successfully locked the account or customer record for exclusive update but the actual write operation to the database subsequently failed. This requires operator notification and likely system investigation to ensure data integrity.

variables.name: XREF-READ-ERROR
variables.description: Error condition indicating that an unexpected system error occurred while reading the card cross-reference file (CARDXREF) during the account lookup process. This is a technical file I/O failure rather than a business data validation error, and prevents the update from proceeding.

variables.name: CODING-TO-BE-DONE
variables.description: Placeholder condition flag marking a section of the program where business logic has not yet been fully implemented. This is a development indicator used by programmers to identify incomplete functionality that still needs to be coded before the program is production-ready.

variables.name: WS-LITERALS
variables.description: Group record containing all fixed constant values used throughout the account update program — including program names, transaction IDs, map names, file names, and character sets used for validation. These literals define the system's navigation targets and reference data used during the update process.

variables.name: LIT-THISPGM
variables.description: The CICS program name of this account update program itself (COACTUPC). Used for self-identification in error messages, communication area routing, and CICS service calls so the system knows which program is currently executing.

variables.name: LIT-THISTRANID
variables.description: The CICS transaction identifier for the account update transaction. This 4-character code is used by CICS to route terminal input to this program and is referenced when the program needs to re-invoke itself after returning control to the operator.

variables.name: LIT-THISMAPSET
variables.description: The BMS mapset name containing the account update screen definition (COACTUP). Used when sending or receiving the account update screen to/from the bank operator's terminal.

variables.name: LIT-THISMAP
variables.description: The specific BMS map name within the mapset that defines the layout of the account update screen. Used in CICS SEND MAP and RECEIVE MAP commands to display and capture the account update form on the operator's terminal.

variables.name: LIT-CARDUPDATE-PGM
variables.description: The CICS program name of the card update program that handles credit card-level detail updates. Used when the account update process needs to transfer control to update card-specific information linked to the account being modified.

variables.name: LIT-CARDUPDATE-TRANID
variables.description: The CICS transaction ID for the card update transaction. Used to initiate or navigate to the card update function when the operator needs to update card-level details (such as expiry or reissue dates) in addition to account information.

variables.name: LIT-CARDUPDATE-MAPSET
variables.description: The BMS mapset name for the card update screen. Referenced when navigating to the card update function so the correct screen layout is displayed to the operator for card-level data entry.

variables.name: LIT-CARDUPDATE-MAP
variables.description: The specific BMS map name for the card update screen within its mapset. Used to display the card update form to the operator when card-level details need to be modified.

variables.name: LIT-CCLISTPGM
variables.description: The CICS program name of the credit card list program. Used when the operator needs to navigate back to the list of credit cards associated with an account, typically after completing or cancelling an update.

variables.name: LIT-CCLISTTRANID
variables.description: The CICS transaction ID for the credit card list transaction. Used to transfer control back to the card listing screen so the operator can select a different card or account to work with.

variables.name: LIT-CCLISTMAPSET
variables.description: The BMS mapset name for the credit card list screen. Referenced when navigating back to the card list display so the correct screen layout is used.

variables.name: LIT-CCLISTMAP
variables.description: The specific BMS map name for the credit card list screen. Used to display the list of cards to the operator when returning from the account update function.

variables.name: LIT-MENUPGM
variables.description: The CICS program name of the main CardDemo menu program. Used when the operator presses a function key to exit the account update screen and return to the main application menu.

variables.name: LIT-MENUTRANID
variables.description: The CICS transaction ID for the main menu transaction. Used to transfer control back to the CardDemo main menu when the operator chooses to exit the account update function.

variables.name: LIT-MENUMAPSET
variables.description: The BMS mapset name for the main menu screen. Referenced when navigating back to the main menu so the correct screen layout is displayed to the operator.

variables.name: LIT-MENUMAP
variables.description: The specific BMS map name for the main menu screen. Used to display the CardDemo main menu to the operator after they exit the account update function.

variables.name: LIT-CARDDTLPGM
variables.description: The CICS program name of the card detail inquiry program. Used when the operator needs to navigate to view detailed information about a specific credit card associated with the account being updated.

variables.name: LIT-CARDDTLTRANID
variables.description: The CICS transaction ID for the card detail inquiry transaction. Used to transfer control to the card detail display when the operator wants to review card-specific information.

variables.name: LIT-CARDDTLMAPSET
variables.description: The BMS mapset name for the card detail screen. Referenced when navigating to the card detail display so the correct screen layout is used to present card information to the operator.

variables.name: LIT-CARDDTLMAP
variables.description: The specific BMS map name for the card detail screen. Used to display detailed credit card information to the operator when they navigate to the card detail inquiry function.

variables.name: LIT-ACCTFILENAME
variables.description: The CICS file name (DDname) of the account master file (ACCTDAT). Used in all CICS file I/O commands (READ, REWRITE) when reading or updating the financial account record — credit limit, balance, and status data.

variables.name: LIT-CUSTFILENAME
variables.description: The CICS file name (DDname) of the customer master file (CUSTDAT). Used in all CICS file I/O commands when reading or updating the customer demographic record — name, address, SSN, date of birth, and phone number.

variables.name: LIT-CARDFILENAME
variables.description: The CICS file name (DDname) of the credit card master file. Used when reading or updating card-level records such as card expiry dates and reissue dates associated with the account being updated.

variables.name: LIT-CARDFILENAME-ACCT-PATH
variables.description: The CICS file name for the alternate index path into the card file keyed by account number. Used to look up credit card records using the account number as the search key, rather than the card number, enabling account-to-card navigation.

variables.name: LIT-CARDXREFNAME-ACCT-PATH
variables.description: The CICS file name for the account-path alternate index into the card cross-reference file (CARDXREF). Used to verify that a valid account-to-card cross-reference record exists before attempting to update account or card data.

variables.name: LIT-ALL-ALPHANUM-FROM-X
variables.description: Group field containing the complete set of valid alphanumeric characters (uppercase letters, lowercase letters, and digits 0-9) used as the source reference in character translation and validation operations for fields such as customer name and address.

variables.name: LIT-ALL-ALPHA-FROM-X
variables.description: Group field containing the complete set of valid alphabetic characters (uppercase and lowercase letters) used as the source reference when validating that customer name fields contain only alphabetic characters, as required by business rules.

variables.name: LIT-UPPER
variables.description: The 26 uppercase letters A through Z, used as a reference string when validating that customer name fields (first, middle, last) contain only alphabetic characters. Part of the character set used in INSPECT or translation operations to enforce the alphabetic-only business rule.

variables.name: LIT-LOWER
variables.description: The 26 lowercase letters a through z, used alongside the uppercase set when validating that customer name fields contain only alphabetic characters. Ensures that names entered in mixed case are accepted as valid.

variables.name: LIT-NUMBERS
variables.description: The 10 numeric digit characters 0 through 9, used as a reference string when validating numeric fields such as SSN segments, phone number segments, and zip codes to ensure they contain only digit characters.

variables.name: LIT-ALL-ALPHA-FROM
variables.description: A 52-character working field (26 uppercase + 26 lowercase letters) used as the 'FROM' argument in character translation operations when validating that customer name fields contain only alphabetic characters. Initialized to spaces and populated at runtime with the valid alpha character set.

variables.name: LIT-ALL-ALPHANUM-FROM
variables.description: A 62-character working field (26 uppercase + 26 lowercase letters + 10 digits) used as the 'FROM' argument in character translation operations when validating that address fields and other alphanumeric fields contain only valid alphanumeric characters.

variables.name: LIT-ALL-NUM-FROM
variables.description: A 10-character working field containing digit characters 0-9, used as the 'FROM' argument in character translation operations when validating purely numeric fields such as SSN segments, phone number parts, and zip codes.

variables.name: LIT-ALPHA-SPACES-TO
variables.description: A 52-character target field of spaces used as the 'TO' argument paired with LIT-ALL-ALPHA-FROM in character translation operations. When translating a name field, any valid alphabetic character maps to a space, leaving only invalid characters visible for detection.

variables.name: LIT-ALPHANUM-SPACES-TO
variables.description: A 62-character target field of spaces used as the 'TO' argument paired with LIT-ALL-ALPHANUM-FROM in character translation operations. Used to detect invalid characters in address and other alphanumeric fields by translating all valid characters to spaces.

variables.name: LIT-NUM-SPACES-TO
variables.description: A 10-character target field of spaces used as the 'TO' argument paired with LIT-ALL-NUM-FROM in character translation operations. Used to detect non-numeric characters in fields like SSN segments and phone number parts by translating all valid digits to spaces.

variables.name: WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA
variables.description: The communication area (COMMAREA) used by this account update program to maintain state between CICS interactions (pseudo-conversational processing). It preserves the current screen data and processing stage across multiple operator interactions with the account update screen.

variables.name: ACCT-UPDATE-SCREEN-DATA
variables.description: Group record within the communication area that holds the current state of the account update screen interaction, tracking what stage of the update process the operator is in — whether account details have been fetched, changes are being entered, or changes are awaiting confirmation.

variables.name: ACUP-CHANGE-ACTION
variables.description: A single-character state indicator that tracks the current stage of the account update workflow. It controls whether the program should fetch and display account details, accept operator changes, or handle validation errors — driving the pseudo-conversational flow of the update process.

variables.name: ACUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED
variables.description: Condition indicating that the account and customer details have not yet been retrieved from the database for display. When true, the program must first look up and display the current account information before the operator can make any changes.

variables.name: ACUP-SHOW-DETAILS
variables.description: Condition (value 'S') indicating that the program is in the 'display details' stage — the account and customer information has been fetched from the database and is being shown to the operator for review before they make any modifications.

variables.name: ACUP-CHANGES-MADE
variables.description: Condition (values 'E' or 'N') indicating that the operator has submitted changes to the account or customer data. The program is now in the validation and update processing stage, regardless of whether the changes passed validation ('N') or failed ('E').

variables.name: ACUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition (value 'E') indicating that the operator's submitted changes failed validation. The screen is redisplayed with error messages highlighting the invalid fields so the operator can correct them before the account update can be written to the database.

variables.name: ACUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED
variables.description: Condition indicating that the bank operator has reviewed the proposed account/customer changes on screen but has NOT yet confirmed them for saving. The update is pending final approval — the system is waiting for the operator to explicitly confirm before writing to the database.

variables.name: ACUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE
variables.description: Condition indicating that the operator confirmed the account/customer changes AND the database update completed successfully. Both the account financial record and the customer demographic record have been saved without error.

variables.name: ACUP-CHANGES-FAILED
variables.description: Composite condition indicating that the confirmed account/customer update attempt failed for any reason — either because the record could not be locked for exclusive update (L) or because the actual write to the database failed (F). Used to trigger error handling and notify the operator that changes were NOT saved.

variables.name: ACUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-LOCK-ERROR
variables.description: Condition indicating that the operator approved the update but the system could not obtain an exclusive lock on the account or customer record — likely because another bank operator or process is simultaneously accessing the same record. The update was blocked to prevent data corruption.

variables.name: ACUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-BUT-FAILED
variables.description: Condition indicating that the operator approved the update and the record was locked, but the actual write operation to the account or customer master file failed due to a system or I/O error. The operator must be informed that despite confirmation, the changes were not persisted.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-DETAILS
variables.description: Group record holding the original 'before-image' snapshot of both the account financial data and the customer demographic data as they existed in the database before the operator made any changes. Used to detect whether any field was actually modified and to support change comparison logic.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-ACCT-DATA
variables.description: Group record holding the original snapshot of all account-level financial fields (account ID, status, balances, limits, dates, group) as read from the account master file before the operator's edits. Used to compare against new values to detect actual changes.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-ACCT-ID-X
variables.description: The original credit card account number (11 characters, alphanumeric format) as it was read from the account master file. Stored as text to allow display and comparison; used to confirm which account record is being updated.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-ACCT-ID
variables.description: Numeric redefinition of the original account number, allowing the program to perform numeric operations or comparisons on the account identifier that was originally stored in text format.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-ACTIVE-STATUS
variables.description: The original active/inactive status of the credit card account as it existed before the operator's update. Valid values are Y (account is active and usable) or N (account is inactive/blocked). Retained to detect if the operator changed the account status.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CURR-BAL
variables.description: The original current outstanding balance on the credit card account, stored as a 12-character text string as read from the database. Retained to detect whether the operator has changed the balance amount during the update session.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CURR-BAL-N
variables.description: Numeric redefinition of the original current balance, allowing arithmetic comparisons or calculations on the balance amount that was stored in text format in the database snapshot.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CREDIT-LIMIT
variables.description: The original total credit limit approved for this credit card account, stored as text as read from the account master file. Used to detect whether the bank operator has changed the customer's borrowing ceiling during the update.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CREDIT-LIMIT-N
variables.description: Numeric redefinition of the original credit limit, enabling numeric comparison or validation of the credit limit value that was stored in text format in the database snapshot.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT
variables.description: The original cash advance credit limit for this account as read from the database — the maximum amount the cardholder is permitted to withdraw as cash. Retained to detect if the operator has modified this sub-limit during the update.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT-N
variables.description: Numeric redefinition of the original cash advance credit limit, allowing numeric operations on the cash limit value that was stored in text format.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-OPEN-DATE
variables.description: The original date on which the credit card account was opened, stored as an 8-character string (YYYYMMDD format) as read from the account master file. Used to detect if the operator has changed the account opening date.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-OPEN-DATE-PARTS
variables.description: Redefinition of the original account open date that breaks it into its individual year, month, and day components, enabling separate validation or comparison of each date part.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-OPEN-YEAR
variables.description: The 4-digit year component of the original account opening date (e.g., 2019). Used to individually validate or compare the year portion of the account open date.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-OPEN-MON
variables.description: The 2-digit month component of the original account opening date (01–12). Used to individually validate or compare the month portion of the account open date.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-OPEN-DAY
variables.description: The 2-digit day component of the original account opening date (01–31). Used to individually validate or compare the day portion of the account open date.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-EXPIRAION-DATE
variables.description: The original expiry date of the credit card as stored in the database (YYYYMMDD format) — the date after which the card is no longer valid for transactions. Retained to detect if the operator has changed the card expiration date.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-EXPIRAION-DATE-PARTS
variables.description: Redefinition of the original card expiry date that splits it into year, month, and day components for individual validation or comparison of each date element.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-EXP-YEAR
variables.description: The 4-digit year component of the original card expiry date (e.g., 2025). Used to individually validate or compare the year the card expires.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-EXP-MON
variables.description: The 2-digit month component of the original card expiry date (01–12). Used to individually validate or compare the month the card expires.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-EXP-DAY
variables.description: The 2-digit day component of the original card expiry date (01–31). Used to individually validate or compare the day the card expires.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-REISSUE-DATE
variables.description: The original date on which the credit card was last reissued or renewed (YYYYMMDD format) as read from the database. Retained to detect if the operator has changed the card renewal date during the update.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-REISSUE-DATE-PARTS
variables.description: Redefinition of the original card reissue date that breaks it into year, month, and day components for individual validation or comparison of each date element.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-REISSUE-YEAR
variables.description: The 4-digit year component of the original card reissue/renewal date. Used to individually validate or compare the year the card was last renewed.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-REISSUE-MON
variables.description: The 2-digit month component of the original card reissue/renewal date (01–12). Used to individually validate or compare the month the card was last renewed.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-REISSUE-DAY
variables.description: The 2-digit day component of the original card reissue/renewal date (01–31). Used to individually validate or compare the day the card was last renewed.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CURR-CYC-CREDIT
variables.description: The original total credit amount posted to the account during the current billing cycle (e.g., payments and refunds), stored as text as read from the database. Retained to detect if the operator has changed this cycle-to-date credit figure.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CURR-CYC-CREDIT-N
variables.description: Numeric redefinition of the original current-cycle credit total, enabling arithmetic operations or numeric comparisons on the cycle credit amount stored in text format.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CURR-CYC-DEBIT
variables.description: The original total debit amount posted to the account during the current billing cycle (e.g., purchases and fees), stored as text as read from the database. Retained to detect if the operator has changed this cycle-to-date debit figure.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CURR-CYC-DEBIT-N
variables.description: Numeric redefinition of the original current-cycle debit total, enabling arithmetic operations or numeric comparisons on the cycle debit amount stored in text format.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-GROUP-ID
variables.description: The original group or product classification code assigned to this credit card account as read from the database (e.g., a portfolio segment or pricing tier identifier). Retained to detect if the operator has changed the account's group assignment.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CUST-DATA
variables.description: Group record holding the original snapshot of all customer demographic fields (name, address, phone, SSN, date of birth, etc.) as read from the customer master file before the operator's edits. Used to compare against new values to detect actual changes to customer information.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CUST-ID-X
variables.description: The original customer identification number (9 characters, alphanumeric format) as read from the customer master file. Links the account record to the specific customer whose personal details are being updated.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CUST-ID
variables.description: Numeric redefinition of the original customer ID, allowing numeric operations or comparisons on the customer identifier that was stored in text format.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CUST-FIRST-NAME
variables.description: The customer's original first (given) name as stored in the customer master file before the update. Retained to detect if the bank operator has changed the customer's first name, which must contain alphabetic characters only.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CUST-MIDDLE-NAME
variables.description: The customer's original middle name as stored in the customer master file before the update. Retained to detect if the bank operator has changed the customer's middle name, which must contain alphabetic characters only.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CUST-LAST-NAME
variables.description: The customer's original last (family) name as stored in the customer master file before the update. Retained to detect if the bank operator has changed the customer's surname, which must contain alphabetic characters only.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CUST-ADDR-LINE-1
variables.description: The first line of the customer's original mailing/residential address (typically street number and street name) as stored in the customer master file. Retained to detect if the operator has updated the customer's primary address line.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CUST-ADDR-LINE-2
variables.description: The second line of the customer's original address (e.g., apartment number, suite, or building name) as stored in the customer master file. Retained to detect if the operator has changed this supplementary address detail.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CUST-ADDR-LINE-3
variables.description: The third line of the customer's original address (typically city name or additional locality information) as stored in the customer master file. Retained to detect if the operator has changed this address component.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CUST-ADDR-STATE-CD
variables.description: The 2-character US state code of the customer's original address (e.g., CA, NY, TX) as stored in the customer master file. Retained to detect if the operator has changed the customer's state of residence.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CUST-ADDR-COUNTRY-CD
variables.description: The 3-character country code of the customer's original address (e.g., USA) as stored in the customer master file. Retained to detect if the operator has changed the customer's country of residence.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CUST-ADDR-ZIP
variables.description: The original postal/ZIP code of the customer's address as stored in the customer master file (up to 10 characters to accommodate ZIP+4 format). Retained to detect if the operator has changed the customer's ZIP code.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CUST-PHONE-NUM-1
variables.description: The customer's original primary phone number as stored in the customer master file, in formatted US phone number layout (e.g., (NXX) NXX-XXXX). Retained to detect if the operator has changed the customer's primary contact number.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CUST-PHONE-NUM-1-X
variables.description: Redefinition of the original primary phone number that breaks it into its individual formatted segments (area code, exchange, and subscriber number) for independent validation of each part of the US phone number.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Formatting character position in the primary phone number — holds the opening parenthesis or separator character before the area code (e.g., '('). Not a data field; purely a display formatting placeholder.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CUST-PHONE-NUM-1A
variables.description: The 3-digit area code segment of the customer's original primary phone number. Validated independently against the list of valid North American Numbering Plan area codes to ensure the phone number is geographically legitimate.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Formatting character position in the primary phone number — holds the separator character between the area code and the exchange (e.g., ')' or '-'). Not a data field; purely a display formatting placeholder.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CUST-PHONE-NUM-1B
variables.description: The 3-digit telephone exchange (central office code) segment of the customer's original primary phone number. Validated independently as a numeric segment to ensure the phone number format is correct.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Formatting character position in the primary phone number — holds the separator character between the exchange and the subscriber number (e.g., '-'). Not a data field; purely a display formatting placeholder.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CUST-PHONE-NUM-1C
variables.description: The 4-digit subscriber number segment of the customer's original primary phone number. Validated independently as a numeric segment to confirm the phone number is properly formatted.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Trailing padding or formatting characters at the end of the primary phone number field (2 characters). Not a data field; used to fill the remaining space in the 15-character phone number layout.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CUST-PHONE-NUM-2
variables.description: The customer's original secondary/alternate phone number as stored in the customer master file, in formatted US phone number layout. Retained to detect if the operator has changed the customer's secondary contact number.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CUST-PHONE-NUM-2-X
variables.description: Redefinition of the original secondary phone number that breaks it into its individual formatted segments (area code, exchange, and subscriber number) for independent validation of each part of the US phone number.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CUST-PHONE-NUM-2A
variables.description: The area code portion (first 3 digits) of the customer's existing phone number as it was stored before any update — used to detect whether the operator has changed the phone area code and to validate it against the North American Numbering Plan (NANP) list of valid area codes.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A separator character (typically a hyphen '-') displayed on screen between the phone area code and the exchange segment of the customer's existing phone number — purely cosmetic, holds no business data.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CUST-PHONE-NUM-2B
variables.description: The telephone exchange (central office code, middle 3 digits) of the customer's existing phone number as previously stored — used to compare against the updated value to detect changes and to validate the exchange segment is numeric.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A separator character (typically a hyphen '-') displayed on screen between the exchange and the subscriber number segments of the customer's existing phone number — purely cosmetic, holds no business data.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CUST-PHONE-NUM-2C
variables.description: The subscriber number (last 4 digits) of the customer's existing phone number as previously stored — used to detect changes made by the operator and to validate the segment is numeric before any update is written.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Padding/spacing characters following the customer's existing phone number on the screen layout — purely cosmetic, holds no business data and ensures correct field alignment on the update screen.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CUST-SSN-X
variables.description: The customer's existing Social Security Number stored as a single 9-character alphanumeric string — represents the original SSN on file before any operator update, used as the baseline for change detection and as the raw input for segment-level validation.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CUST-SSN
variables.description: A structured redefinition of the customer's existing 9-digit Social Security Number that breaks it into its three regulatory segments (3-2-4 digits) — allows the program to independently validate each SSN segment against business rules (e.g., Part 1 cannot be 000, 666, or 900-999) without altering the stored raw value.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CUST-GOVT-ISSUED-ID
variables.description: The customer's existing government-issued identification number (such as a passport number or national ID) as currently stored on file — retained as the original value to detect whether the operator has changed this identity document reference during the update.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CUST-DOB-YYYY-MM-DD
variables.description: The customer's existing date of birth stored as a single 8-character string in YYYYMMDD format — represents the original birth date on file before any operator update, used as the baseline for change detection and as the raw value for calendar validation.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CUST-DOB-PARTS
variables.description: A structured redefinition of the customer's existing date of birth that splits it into year, month, and day components — enables the program to independently validate each date part (e.g., month must be 01-12, day must be valid for the given month) against business rules before allowing an update.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CUST-DOB-YEAR
variables.description: The 4-digit birth year component of the customer's existing date of birth — independently validated to ensure it represents a plausible past year (the customer must have been born before the current date).

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CUST-DOB-MON
variables.description: The 2-digit birth month component of the customer's existing date of birth — independently validated to ensure it falls within the range 01 through 12 as part of the composite date-of-birth validation.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CUST-DOB-DAY
variables.description: The 2-digit birth day component of the customer's existing date of birth — independently validated to ensure it is a valid calendar day for the given month and year as part of the composite date-of-birth validation.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CUST-EFT-ACCOUNT-ID
variables.description: The customer's existing Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) bank account identifier as currently stored — represents the linked external bank account used for payments or direct debits, retained as the original value to detect whether the operator has changed the customer's EFT account reference.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CUST-PRI-HOLDER-IND
variables.description: An indicator flag showing whether the customer is the primary cardholder on the account as currently recorded — distinguishes primary account holders from secondary/authorized users, retained as the original value to detect any change made by the operator.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CUST-FICO-SCORE-X
variables.description: The customer's existing FICO credit score stored as a 3-character alphanumeric string — represents the creditworthiness score on file before any update, used as the baseline for change detection and as the raw input for numeric validation.

variables.name: ACUP-OLD-CUST-FICO-SCORE
variables.description: A numeric redefinition of the customer's existing FICO credit score — allows the program to treat the score as a numeric value for range validation (e.g., must be a valid score between 300 and 850) while the alphanumeric version is used for screen display and change detection.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-DETAILS
variables.description: The top-level grouping of all new (updated) values entered by the bank operator on the account update screen — contains both the revised financial account data and the revised customer demographic data that will replace the existing records if all validations pass.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-ACCT-DATA
variables.description: The grouping of all new financial account fields entered by the operator — encompasses the updated account identifier, status, balances, credit limits, and key dates that will be written to the credit card account master record (CVACT01Y) if validation succeeds.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-ACCT-ID-X
variables.description: The account number entered by the operator on the update screen, stored as an 11-character alphanumeric string — identifies which credit card account record is to be updated and is validated to confirm the account exists in the master file before any changes are applied.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-ACCT-ID
variables.description: A numeric redefinition of the new account number — allows the program to treat the account identifier as a numeric value for lookup and comparison operations against the account master file while the alphanumeric version is used for screen handling.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-ACTIVE-STATUS
variables.description: The updated account active/inactive status entered by the operator — must be exactly 'Y' (account is active and can be used for transactions) or 'N' (account is inactive/blocked); any other value is rejected as a validation error per business rules.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CURR-BAL
variables.description: The updated current outstanding balance on the credit card account as entered by the operator, stored as a 12-character alphanumeric string — represents the total amount the cardholder currently owes; validated to be a valid signed numeric amount before being written to the account master record.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CURR-BAL-N
variables.description: A numeric redefinition of the updated current balance field — allows the program to perform arithmetic validation and comparison on the balance amount while the alphanumeric version is used for screen input/output handling.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CREDIT-LIMIT
variables.description: The updated total credit limit for the account as entered by the operator — defines the maximum amount the cardholder is permitted to charge on the card; validated as a valid signed numeric amount before being written to the account master record.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CREDIT-LIMIT-N
variables.description: A numeric redefinition of the updated credit limit field — allows the program to perform numeric validation and business rule checks (e.g., cash credit limit must not exceed total credit limit) while the alphanumeric version handles screen display.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT
variables.description: The updated cash advance credit limit for the account as entered by the operator — defines the maximum amount the cardholder may withdraw as a cash advance; validated as a valid signed numeric amount and must not exceed the total credit limit.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT-N
variables.description: A numeric redefinition of the updated cash advance credit limit — allows the program to perform numeric validation and comparison against the total credit limit while the alphanumeric version handles screen input/output.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-OPEN-DATE
variables.description: The updated account opening date as entered by the operator, stored as an 8-character string in YYYYMMDD format — records when the credit card account was originally established; validated as a valid calendar date before being written to the account master record.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-OPEN-DATE-PARTS
variables.description: A structured redefinition of the updated account opening date that splits it into year, month, and day components — enables independent validation of each date part to ensure the opening date is a valid calendar date before the account record is updated.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-OPEN-YEAR
variables.description: The 4-digit year component of the updated account opening date — independently validated as part of the composite opening date validation to ensure the account establishment year is a plausible value.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-OPEN-MON
variables.description: The 2-digit month component of the updated account opening date — independently validated to ensure it falls within the range 01 through 12 as part of the composite opening date validation.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-OPEN-DAY
variables.description: The 2-digit day component of the updated account opening date — independently validated to ensure it is a valid calendar day for the given month and year as part of the composite opening date validation.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-EXPIRAION-DATE
variables.description: The updated credit card expiry date as entered by the operator, stored as an 8-character string in YYYYMMDD format — defines when the physical card expires and becomes invalid for transactions; validated as a valid future calendar date before being written to the card record.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-EXPIRAION-DATE-PARTS
variables.description: A structured redefinition of the updated card expiry date that splits it into year, month, and day components — enables independent validation of each date part to confirm the expiry date is a valid future calendar date before the card record is updated.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-EXP-YEAR
variables.description: The 4-digit year component of the updated card expiry date — independently validated to ensure the expiry year is in the future relative to the current system date, confirming the card will still be valid.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-EXP-MON
variables.description: The 2-digit month component of the updated card expiry date — independently validated to ensure it falls within the range 01 through 12 as part of the composite expiry date validation.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-EXP-DAY
variables.description: The 2-digit day component of the updated card expiry date — independently validated to ensure it is a valid calendar day for the given month and year as part of the composite expiry date validation.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-REISSUE-DATE
variables.description: The updated card reissue/renewal date as entered by the operator, stored as an 8-character string in YYYYMMDD format — records when the card was most recently reissued or renewed to the cardholder; validated as a valid calendar date before being written to the card record.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-REISSUE-DATE-PARTS
variables.description: A structured redefinition of the updated card reissue date that splits it into year, month, and day components — enables independent validation of each date part to confirm the reissue date is a valid calendar date before the card record is updated.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-REISSUE-YEAR
variables.description: The 4-digit year component of the updated card reissue date — independently validated as part of the composite reissue date validation to ensure the card renewal year is a plausible value.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-REISSUE-MON
variables.description: The 2-digit month component of the updated card reissue date — independently validated to ensure it falls within the range 01 through 12 as part of the composite reissue date validation.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-REISSUE-DAY
variables.description: The 2-digit day component of the updated card reissue date — independently validated to ensure it is a valid calendar day for the given month and year as part of the composite reissue date validation.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CURR-CYC-CREDIT
variables.description: The updated total credit amount posted to the account in the current billing cycle as entered by the operator — represents payments, refunds, and other credits applied during the current statement period; validated as a valid signed numeric amount before being written to the account master record.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CURR-CYC-CREDIT-N
variables.description: A numeric redefinition of the updated current cycle credit amount — allows the program to perform numeric validation and arithmetic operations on the cycle credit value while the alphanumeric version handles screen input/output.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CURR-CYC-DEBIT
variables.description: The updated total debit amount posted to the account in the current billing cycle as entered by the operator — represents purchases, fees, and other charges applied during the current statement period; validated as a valid signed numeric amount before being written to the account master record.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CURR-CYC-DEBIT-N
variables.description: A numeric redefinition of the updated current cycle debit amount — allows the program to perform numeric validation and arithmetic operations on the cycle debit value while the alphanumeric version handles screen input/output.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-GROUP-ID
variables.description: The updated account group or portfolio identifier as entered by the operator — categorizes the credit card account into a business segment or product group (e.g., a specific card product tier or customer segment), used for reporting and account management purposes.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CUST-DATA
variables.description: The grouping of all new customer demographic fields entered by the operator — encompasses the updated customer identifier, name, address, and identity information that will be written to the customer master record (CVCUS01Y) if all validations pass alongside the account update.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CUST-ID-X
variables.description: The customer number entered by the operator on the update screen, stored as a 9-character alphanumeric string — identifies which customer master record is linked to the account being updated and is validated to confirm the customer exists before any changes are applied.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CUST-ID
variables.description: A numeric redefinition of the new customer number — allows the program to treat the customer identifier as a numeric value for lookup and comparison operations against the customer master file while the alphanumeric version handles screen display.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CUST-FIRST-NAME
variables.description: The updated first (given) name of the customer as entered by the operator — must contain alphabetic characters only per business rules; validated before being written to the customer master record to ensure the cardholder's legal name is correctly recorded.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CUST-MIDDLE-NAME
variables.description: The updated middle name of the customer as entered by the operator — must contain alphabetic characters only per business rules; validated before being written to the customer master record to support full legal name identification of the cardholder.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CUST-LAST-NAME
variables.description: The updated last (family/surname) name of the customer as entered by the operator — must contain alphabetic characters only per business rules; validated before being written to the customer master record to ensure the cardholder's legal surname is correctly recorded.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CUST-ADDR-LINE-1
variables.description: The first line of the customer's updated mailing address as entered by the operator (typically the street number and street name) — validated to contain alphanumeric characters before being written to the customer master record; used for statement delivery and correspondence.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CUST-ADDR-LINE-2
variables.description: The second line of the customer's updated mailing address as entered by the operator (typically apartment, suite, or unit number) — validated to contain alphanumeric characters before being written to the customer master record; supplements the primary address line for accurate mail delivery.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CUST-ADDR-LINE-3
variables.description: The third line of the customer's updated mailing address as entered by the operator (typically the city and/or additional locality information) — validated to contain alphanumeric characters before being written to the customer master record.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CUST-ADDR-STATE-CD
variables.description: The 2-character US state code of the customer's updated address as entered by the operator (e.g., 'CA' for California, 'NY' for New York) — validated against the list of valid US state codes before being written to the customer master record to ensure accurate geographic identification for the cardholder.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CUST-ADDR-COUNTRY-CD
variables.description: The 3-character country code of the customer's updated address as entered by the operator (e.g., 'USA') — validated to contain alphanumeric characters before being written to the customer master record; identifies the country of residence for the cardholder for regulatory and correspondence purposes.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CUST-ADDR-ZIP
variables.description: The updated ZIP/postal code for the customer's mailing address, as entered by the bank operator on the account update screen. Used to ensure mail, statements, and correspondence reach the correct location. Subject to alphanumeric validation as part of the address field business rules.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CUST-PHONE-NUM-1
variables.description: The customer's primary phone number as a single formatted string (e.g. NXX-NXX-XXXX), entered by the bank operator. This is the main contact number stored on the customer demographic record and used for account communications. The full 15-character field accommodates the formatted display including separators and trailing spaces.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CUST-PHONE-NUM-1-X
variables.description: A structured overlay of the primary phone number field that breaks the formatted phone string into its individual components for validation. Allows the program to independently validate the area code, exchange, and subscriber number segments of the primary contact phone number against US phone format rules.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A separator character position (typically a parenthesis or dash) before the area code in the formatted primary phone number display. Not used in business logic — purely a formatting placeholder to align with the displayed phone number format on screen.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CUST-PHONE-NUM-1A
variables.description: The 3-digit area code portion of the customer's primary phone number. Independently validated against the list of valid North American Numbering Plan (NANP) area codes to ensure the phone number belongs to a real geographic or service region.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A separator character position (typically a dash or closing parenthesis) between the area code and exchange segments of the primary phone number. Not used in business logic — purely a formatting placeholder.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CUST-PHONE-NUM-1B
variables.description: The 3-digit telephone exchange (central office code) portion of the customer's primary phone number. Validated as numeric and non-blank as part of the US phone number format business rules.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A separator character position (typically a dash) between the exchange and subscriber number segments of the primary phone number. Not used in business logic — purely a formatting placeholder.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CUST-PHONE-NUM-1C
variables.description: The 4-digit subscriber number (line number) portion of the customer's primary phone number. Validated as numeric and non-blank as part of the US phone number format business rules.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Two trailing padding characters at the end of the primary phone number structured overlay. Not used in business logic — accommodates the full 15-character field width after the 10 digits and 3 separators are accounted for.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CUST-PHONE-NUM-2
variables.description: The customer's secondary (alternate) phone number as a single formatted string, entered by the bank operator. This may represent a home, work, or mobile number alternative to the primary contact number, stored on the customer demographic record for additional contact options.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CUST-PHONE-NUM-2-X
variables.description: A structured overlay of the secondary phone number field that breaks the formatted phone string into its individual components for validation. Allows the program to independently validate the area code, exchange, and subscriber number segments of the alternate contact phone number against US phone format rules.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A separator character position before the area code in the formatted secondary phone number display. Not used in business logic — purely a formatting placeholder.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CUST-PHONE-NUM-2A
variables.description: The 3-digit area code portion of the customer's secondary phone number. Independently validated against the list of valid North American Numbering Plan (NANP) area codes to ensure the alternate phone number belongs to a real geographic or service region.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A separator character position between the area code and exchange segments of the secondary phone number. Not used in business logic — purely a formatting placeholder.
