variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CUST-PHONE-NUM-2B
variables.description: The 3-digit telephone exchange portion of the customer's secondary phone number. Validated as numeric and non-blank as part of the US phone number format business rules.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A separator character position between the exchange and subscriber number segments of the secondary phone number. Not used in business logic — purely a formatting placeholder.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CUST-PHONE-NUM-2C
variables.description: The 4-digit subscriber number portion of the customer's secondary phone number. Validated as numeric and non-blank as part of the US phone number format business rules.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Two trailing padding characters at the end of the secondary phone number structured overlay. Not used in business logic — accommodates the full 15-character field width after the 10 digits and 3 separators are accounted for.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CUST-SSN-X
variables.description: The customer's Social Security Number broken into its three standard segments for individual validation. The SSN is a mandatory government-issued identifier used to uniquely identify the customer for regulatory, credit reporting, and identity verification purposes. Each segment is validated independently per IRS/SSA rules.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CUST-SSN-1
variables.description: The first 3-digit segment (Area Number) of the customer's Social Security Number. Per business rules, this segment cannot be '000', '666', or any value in the range 900-999, as these are invalid SSN prefixes per Social Security Administration rules. Failure to pass this check blocks the account update.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CUST-SSN-2
variables.description: The middle 2-digit segment (Group Number) of the customer's Social Security Number. Must be numeric and non-zero per business validation rules. An invalid group number prevents the customer record from being updated.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CUST-SSN-3
variables.description: The last 4-digit segment (Serial Number) of the customer's Social Security Number. Must be numeric and non-zero per business validation rules. An invalid serial number prevents the customer record from being updated.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CUST-SSN
variables.description: An alternate view of the customer's Social Security Number as a single contiguous 9-digit value, overlaying the three-segment SSN structure. Used when the SSN needs to be read or written as a complete identifier rather than in its validated segments — for example, when storing to or retrieving from the customer master record.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CUST-GOVT-ISSUED-ID
variables.description: A government-issued identification number for the customer other than the SSN — for example, a passport number, driver's license number, or national ID. Stored on the customer demographic record to support identity verification and regulatory compliance requirements for non-SSN identification scenarios.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CUST-DOB-YYYY-MM-DD
variables.description: The customer's date of birth stored as a single 8-character string in YYYYMMDD format, as entered by the bank operator. Used for identity verification, age eligibility checks, and regulatory compliance. The date must represent a valid past calendar date and is subject to full date validation.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CUST-DOB-PARTS
variables.description: A structured overlay of the customer's date of birth field that splits the date into its year, month, and day components for independent validation. Allows the program to separately verify that the birth year, birth month, and birth day are each individually valid calendar values, as required by the date-of-birth business validation rules.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CUST-DOB-YEAR
variables.description: The 4-digit birth year component of the customer's date of birth (e.g. 1975). Validated independently to ensure it represents a plausible past year — must be a valid numeric year that, combined with month and day, produces a date in the past relative to the current system date.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CUST-DOB-MON
variables.description: The 2-digit birth month component of the customer's date of birth (01-12). Validated independently to ensure it is a valid calendar month. An invalid month value (e.g. 00 or 13) will cause the date-of-birth validation to fail and block the customer record update.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CUST-DOB-DAY
variables.description: The 2-digit birth day component of the customer's date of birth (01-31, depending on month). Validated independently to ensure it is a valid day for the given month and year. An invalid day value will cause the date-of-birth validation to fail and block the customer record update.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CUST-EFT-ACCOUNT-ID
variables.description: The customer's Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) bank account identifier — the external bank account number linked to this credit card customer for purposes such as automatic payment, direct debit, or refund processing. Stored on the customer demographic record to enable automated payment transactions.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CUST-PRI-HOLDER-IND
variables.description: An indicator flag that identifies whether this customer is the primary account holder (as opposed to a secondary or authorized user). Determines the customer's legal and financial responsibility level for the credit card account — the primary holder bears full liability for the account balance.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CUST-FICO-SCORE-X
variables.description: The customer's FICO credit score stored as a 3-character alphanumeric string, as entered by the bank operator. The FICO score is a key creditworthiness indicator used in credit risk assessment and account management decisions. This character version is used for screen display and input capture before numeric validation.

variables.name: ACUP-NEW-CUST-FICO-SCORE
variables.description: A numeric overlay of the customer's FICO credit score field, allowing the program to perform numeric range validation on the score value. The FICO score must fall within the valid industry range (300 to 850) to be accepted — scores outside this range indicate a data entry error and will block the customer record update.

variables.name: FICO-RANGE-IS-VALID
variables.description: A condition name that evaluates to TRUE when the customer's FICO credit score falls within the valid industry range of 300 to 850. Used by the validation logic to quickly determine whether the entered FICO score is a legitimate creditworthiness value. A score outside this range is flagged as invalid, preventing the customer record from being updated with an implausible credit score.

variables.name: WS-COMMAREA
variables.description: The working storage communication area used to pass context and data between this account update program and other CICS programs in the CardDemo application (such as the calling menu or inquiry program). Holds up to 2000 characters of shared state information including account identifiers, navigation flags, and operator context needed to maintain continuity across program-to-program transfers.

variables.name: DFHCOMMAREA
variables.description: The standard CICS communication area passed to this program when it is invoked by another program or by a CICS RETURN/XCTL command. Contains the data handed off from the previous program in the transaction flow — for example, the account number selected for update from the account inquiry screen. CICS automatically maps this area when the program is called.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A single-character padding or reserved field within the CICS communication area passed to this program. Not directly used in business logic — serves as a structural placeholder, possibly to align subsequent fields or to accommodate a version/type indicator byte at the start of the communication area.

paragraphs.name: 0000-MAIN
paragraphs.description: This is the main orchestration paragraph that controls the entire account update transaction lifecycle — from initial entry and session setup, through function key routing, to validation and screen presentation. It determines what action to take based on how the operator arrived at the screen and what key they pressed, directing the flow to the appropriate processing step.

paragraphs.name: COMMON-RETURN
paragraphs.description: COMMON-RETURN is the standard exit routine that concludes any interaction with the account update screen. It packages any message to display to the operator, preserves the full session context, and hands control back to the CICS transaction manager — keeping the transaction alive and ready to receive the operator's next action.

paragraphs.name: 0000-MAIN-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point of the main processing routine, marking the boundary where the account update transaction's primary logic concludes and control is returned to the CICS transaction manager.

paragraphs.name: 1000-PROCESS-INPUTS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph orchestrates the complete input processing cycle for the account update screen: it collects the operator's entered changes, validates them against all business rules, and prepares the screen to redisplay with any resulting error messages or confirmation, keeping the operator in the update transaction.

paragraphs.name: 1000-PROCESS-INPUTS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the designated exit point for the input processing routine, allowing the program to cleanly conclude all input validation and data change detection steps before returning control to the main processing flow.

paragraphs.name: 1100-RECEIVE-MAP
paragraphs.description: This paragraph captures all data entered by the bank operator on the account update screen and stages it for validation and processing. It reads every editable field — covering both financial account attributes and customer demographic details — and normalises blank or placeholder entries before passing the collected data forward for business rule validation.

paragraphs.name: 1100-RECEIVE-MAP-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as a formal exit point for the screen data reception routine, allowing the program to cleanly return control to the calling logic after all operator-entered account and customer update data has been received from the screen.

paragraphs.name: 1200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph orchestrates the full validation of all account and customer fields entered by the bank operator on the update screen. It determines whether the submission contains real changes, then systematically validates every financial and demographic field before deciding if the update is safe to proceed.

paragraphs.name: 1200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the entire input validation routine. It marks the boundary where all account and customer field validations have been completed and control is returned to the main processing flow.

paragraphs.name: 1205-COMPARE-OLD-NEW
paragraphs.description: This paragraph determines whether the bank operator has actually made any changes to the account or customer data by comparing every submitted field against the original values loaded from the database. If no differences are detected across all financial account attributes and customer demographic details, the transaction is flagged as a no-change submission, preventing an unnecessary and potentially misleading database write.

paragraphs.name: 1205-COMPARE-OLD-NEW-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the old-versus-new data comparison routine, marking the end of the process that determines whether the operator has actually changed any account or customer information. It acts as a structural boundary, ensuring control returns cleanly to the calling logic after the change-detection check is complete.

paragraphs.name: 1210-EDIT-ACCOUNT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph validates the account number entered by the bank operator on the update screen, ensuring it is present, fully numeric, and non-zero before allowing the account update to proceed. It acts as the first gate in the update workflow — rejecting blank or malformed account identifiers before any database lookup or record modification is attempted.

paragraphs.name: 1210-EDIT-ACCOUNT-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the account field validation routine, marking the boundary where account data validation concludes and control returns to the calling process. It is a structural terminator with no business logic of its own.

paragraphs.name: 1215-EDIT-MANDATORY
paragraphs.description: This paragraph enforces that a mandatory field on the account/customer update screen has actually been filled in by the bank operator. It detects blank or empty submissions for required fields and raises a specific 'field not supplied' error, preventing the update from proceeding with missing critical data.

paragraphs.name: 1215-EDIT-MANDATORY-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the mandatory field validation routine. It marks the end of the validation block that checks all required fields have been populated before allowing the account update to proceed.

paragraphs.name: 1220-EDIT-YESNO
paragraphs.description: This paragraph validates that a Yes/No field (such as account active status) has been supplied and contains only an acceptable value of 'Y' or 'N'. It enforces the business rule that binary status indicators cannot be left blank or set to an unrecognised value, flagging any violation with an appropriate error message for the operator.

paragraphs.name: 1220-EDIT-YESNO-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the Yes/No account status validation routine. It marks the end of the validation logic that checks whether the account active/inactive status field contains only permitted values.

paragraphs.name: 1225-EDIT-ALPHA-REQD
paragraphs.description: This paragraph validates that a mandatory customer or account text field (such as a name component or address element) has been provided and contains only alphabetic characters. It enforces two distinct business rules: the field must not be blank, and it must not contain numeric digits or special characters.

paragraphs.name: 1225-EDIT-ALPHA-REQD-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the alphabetic field validation routine, marking the end of the process that checks whether customer name or other alphabetic fields contain only valid alphabetic characters. It is a structural boundary that allows the program to cleanly return control to whichever part of the update workflow invoked the validation check.

paragraphs.name: 1230-EDIT-ALPHANUM-REQD
paragraphs.description: This paragraph validates that a required alphanumeric field (such as an address line, city, or zip code) has been supplied by the operator and contains only letters, digits, and spaces. It enforces two distinct business rules: the field must not be blank, and it must not contain special characters or symbols.

paragraphs.name: 1230-EDIT-ALPHANUM-REQD-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the alphanumeric required-field validation routine. It marks the end of the validation logic that checks whether mandatory alphanumeric fields (such as address lines, city, state, zip code, and country) have been populated with acceptable characters, allowing the program to return control to the calling validation process.

paragraphs.name: 1235-EDIT-ALPHA-OPT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph validates that an optional customer text field (such as a name component or address element) contains only alphabetic characters and spaces, or is left intentionally blank. It enforces the business rule that certain demographic fields must not contain numeric digits or special characters, while also permitting the field to be omitted entirely.

paragraphs.name: 1235-EDIT-ALPHA-OPT-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the designated exit point for the optional alphabetic field validation routine. It provides a clean termination anchor that other parts of the validation logic can branch to when optional alpha field checks are complete or need to be bypassed.

paragraphs.name: 1240-EDIT-ALPHANUM-OPT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph validates that an optional alphanumeric field entered by bank staff contains only letters, digits, and spaces — but treats a completely blank or absent entry as acceptable, since the field is not mandatory. It is reused across multiple address and name fields on the account update screen.

paragraphs.name: 1240-EDIT-ALPHANUM-OPT-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the designated exit point for the optional alphanumeric field validation routine, allowing the validation logic to cleanly conclude and return control to the calling process after optional address or name fields have been checked.

paragraphs.name: 1245-EDIT-NUM-REQD
paragraphs.description: This paragraph validates that a required numeric field submitted by the bank operator is present, contains only digits, and is not zero. It enforces mandatory numeric input rules for fields such as SSN segments, phone number segments, or similar identifier components before any account or customer update is committed.

paragraphs.name: 1245-EDIT-NUM-REQD-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the numeric field validation routine, allowing the program to cleanly return control to whichever validation step invoked the numeric check, after determining whether a required numeric field was blank or invalid.

paragraphs.name: 1250-EDIT-SIGNED-9V2
paragraphs.description: This paragraph validates that a monetary amount field (such as credit limit, balance, or cycle credits/debits) entered by the bank operator is both present and formatted as a valid signed numeric currency value. It enforces that no financial amount field is left blank or contains non-numeric, non-currency characters before the account update is allowed to proceed.

paragraphs.name: 1250-EDIT-SIGNED-9V2-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the signed numeric amount validation routine. It marks the end of the validation logic for financial fields such as credit limits, balances, and cycle amounts, allowing the program to return control to whichever validation step invoked it.

paragraphs.name: 1260-EDIT-US-PHONE-NUM
paragraphs.description: This paragraph validates the customer's US phone number entered on the account update screen. It begins by assuming the phone number is invalid, then immediately grants an exception if all three segments of the phone number are entirely blank — because providing a phone number is optional for the customer record.

paragraphs.name: EDIT-AREA-CODE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph validates the area code portion of a customer's US phone number, ensuring it is present, fully numeric, non-zero, and recognised as a legitimate North American general-purpose area code before the full phone number is accepted.

paragraphs.name: EDIT-US-PHONE-PREFIX
paragraphs.description: This paragraph validates the telephone exchange prefix (middle segment) of a customer's US phone number, ensuring it is present, purely numeric, and non-zero before the full phone number can be accepted. It enforces North American telephone numbering standards at the exchange-code level to guarantee the stored contact number is reachable and correctly formatted.

paragraphs.name: EDIT-US-PHONE-LINENUM
paragraphs.description: This paragraph validates the subscriber line number segment (last 4 digits) of a US phone number entered by bank staff. It ensures the segment is present, fully numeric, and non-zero before the phone number can be accepted as valid on the account update screen.

paragraphs.name: EDIT-US-PHONE-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the US phone number validation routine. It marks the end of the phone number validation process, returning control to whichever part of the program invoked the validation check.

paragraphs.name: 1260-EDIT-US-PHONE-NUM-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the US phone number validation routine, marking the end of the phone number format checking process and returning control to the calling logic.

paragraphs.name: 1265-EDIT-US-SSN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph validates the customer's US Social Security Number entered by the bank operator, checking each of the three segments (area, group, and serial numbers) independently for correct format, numeric content, and compliance with SSN issuance rules that prohibit certain reserved or invalid number ranges.

paragraphs.name: 1265-EDIT-US-SSN-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the US Social Security Number validation routine. It marks the end of the SSN editing process, allowing control to return to whichever part of the program invoked the SSN validation.

paragraphs.name: 1270-EDIT-US-STATE-CD
paragraphs.description: This paragraph validates that the US state code entered by the bank operator for the customer's address is a recognised and legitimate US state abbreviation. If the state code is invalid, the update is blocked and a descriptive error message is generated for the operator.

paragraphs.name: 1270-EDIT-US-STATE-CD-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the US state code validation routine, marking the end of the state code checking process and returning control to the calling logic within the account update workflow.

paragraphs.name: 1275-EDIT-FICO-SCORE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph validates that the customer's FICO credit score falls within the accepted industry range of 300 to 850. If the score is outside this range, the update is rejected and an error message is generated for the bank operator.

paragraphs.name: 1275-EDIT-FICO-SCORE-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the FICO credit score validation routine, marking the end of that validation step and returning control to the calling logic so processing can continue. It acts as a structured boundary that cleanly closes the FICO score editing section before the program moves on to address validation.

paragraphs.name: 1280-EDIT-US-STATE-ZIP-CD
paragraphs.description: This paragraph validates that the customer's US state code and ZIP code are geographically consistent with each other — ensuring that the first two digits of the ZIP code actually belong to the entered state, preventing mismatched address data from being saved to the customer record.

paragraphs.name: 1280-EDIT-US-STATE-ZIP-CD-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the US state and ZIP code validation routine, marking the end of that validation block and returning control to the calling logic within the account update process.

paragraphs.name: 2000-DECIDE-ACTION
paragraphs.description: This paragraph acts as the central workflow controller for the account update transaction, routing the operator's session to the correct next step based on the current screen state and the action key pressed. It governs the full lifecycle of an update: from initial data retrieval, through validation, confirmation, and final save, to post-save reset.

paragraphs.name: 2000-DECIDE-ACTION-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the action-decision routing logic, marking the end of the section that determines which processing path to follow based on operator input and screen state. It contains no business logic itself, acting purely as a structural boundary that signals the completion of the decision-routing section.

paragraphs.name: 3000-SEND-MAP
paragraphs.description: Orchestrates the complete preparation and delivery of the account update screen to the bank operator's terminal. It coordinates all steps needed to render a fully populated, validated, and properly formatted screen — from initialising the display layout to transmitting the final output.

paragraphs.name: 3000-SEND-MAP-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the screen-sending routine, marking the end of the process that presents the account update screen to the bank operator. It acts as a structural boundary in the program flow, ensuring control returns cleanly to the calling logic after the screen display operation is complete.

paragraphs.name: 3100-SCREEN-INIT
paragraphs.description: Initialises the account update screen by clearing all previous display content and populating the standard screen header fields — titles, transaction identity, program identity, and the current date and time — so that bank staff see a clean, correctly labelled screen before any account data is loaded.

paragraphs.name: 3100-SCREEN-INIT-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the screen initialisation routine, marking the boundary where screen setup processing ends and control returns to the calling logic. It contains no business logic itself, acting purely as a structural terminator for the initialisation phase.

paragraphs.name: 3200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph controls what account and customer data is displayed on the update screen, determining whether to show a blank entry form, the original fetched record, or the operator's in-progress edits based on the current state of the transaction. It acts as the screen rendering decision hub, ensuring the operator always sees the correct version of the data for their current step in the update workflow.

paragraphs.name: 3200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as a formal exit point for the screen variable setup routine, marking the end of the process that prepares account and customer data fields for display on the update screen. It contains no business logic itself, acting purely as a structural terminator that allows other parts of the program to branch here cleanly after screen preparation is complete.

paragraphs.name: 3201-SHOW-INITIAL-VALUES
paragraphs.description: This paragraph initializes the account update screen by clearing all displayed fields to a blank/empty state before populating them with current data from the database. It ensures the operator sees a clean, consistent screen with no residual values from any previous transaction.

paragraphs.name: 3201-SHOW-INITIAL-VALUES-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as a formal exit point for the routine that populates the account update screen with existing account and customer data. It acts as a structural boundary marker, allowing the program to cleanly return control to the calling logic after the screen pre-population process is complete.

paragraphs.name: 3202-SHOW-ORIGINAL-VALUES
paragraphs.description: This paragraph populates the account update screen with the current on-file values for both the financial account and the linked customer profile, so that bank staff can see the existing data before making changes. It resets all non-key screen field indicators to a neutral state and signals the screen to prompt the operator for edits.

paragraphs.name: 3202-SHOW-ORIGINAL-VALUES-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as a formal exit point for the routine that restores and displays the original account and customer data on screen. It contains no logic itself, acting purely as a structural terminator that returns control to the calling routine.

paragraphs.name: 3203-SHOW-UPDATED-VALUES
paragraphs.description: This paragraph refreshes the account update screen with the operator's newly entered values, ready for display after validation. It ensures that both valid (numerically formatted) and invalid (as-entered) financial amounts are shown correctly, while all customer demographic and account date fields are always reflected exactly as submitted.

paragraphs.name: 3203-SHOW-UPDATED-VALUES-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as a formal exit point for the routine that displays refreshed account and customer data on the update screen after changes have been applied. It acts as a structural boundary marker, allowing other parts of the program to transfer control back cleanly once the screen refresh logic is complete.

paragraphs.name: 3250-SETUP-INFOMSG
paragraphs.description: This paragraph determines the appropriate guidance message to display to the bank operator based on the current state of the account update transaction, then places both the instructional message and any error/return message onto the screen for the operator to read.

paragraphs.name: 3250-SETUP-INFOMSG-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as a formal exit point for the informational message setup routine, marking the end of the process that prepares status or error messages for display to the bank operator. It contains no business logic itself, acting purely as a structural terminator for the message preparation flow.

paragraphs.name: 3300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph controls the visual presentation of the account update screen by determining which fields the operator can edit versus which are locked, positioning the cursor on the first field requiring attention, and applying colour-coded highlighting to signal validation errors — ensuring the operator is guided efficiently to correct any invalid or missing data before the update is saved.

paragraphs.name: 3300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the screen attribute setup routine, marking the end of the process that configures field highlighting, protection, and display properties on the account update screen. It contains no business logic itself, acting purely as a structural boundary that allows other parts of the program to transfer control cleanly after screen formatting is complete.

paragraphs.name: 3310-PROTECT-ALL-ATTRS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph locks every editable field on the account update screen, making the entire form read-only so that bank staff cannot modify any account or customer data. It is invoked when the screen must be displayed in a view-only state — for example, during confirmation steps or when the operator does not have permission to edit.

paragraphs.name: 3310-PROTECT-ALL-ATTRS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the routine that locks all screen fields against further operator input. It marks the end of the field-protection logic, allowing the program to return control to the calling routine after all screen attributes have been set to read-only.

paragraphs.name: 3320-UNPROTECT-FEW-ATTRS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph configures the account update screen so that bank staff can edit most account and customer fields, while locking down a small number of sensitive or system-controlled fields (such as the customer number and country) to prevent unauthorised modification. It establishes the correct mix of editable and protected fields before the screen is presented to the operator.

paragraphs.name: 3320-UNPROTECT-FEW-ATTRS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as a structural exit point for the screen field unprotection routine, allowing the program to cleanly return control after selectively enabling operator editing on specific screen fields. It contains no business logic itself, acting purely as a labeled return marker.

paragraphs.name: 3390-SETUP-INFOMSG-ATTRS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph configures the visual presentation of the account update screen by setting the display attributes of the informational message area and function key indicators based on the current state of the transaction — whether a message exists, whether changes are pending confirmation, or whether the operator has already completed an update.

paragraphs.name: 3390-SETUP-INFOMSG-ATTRS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as a formal exit point for the informational message attribute setup routine. It marks the end of the screen field highlighting and status display configuration process, returning control to the calling logic after all screen presentation attributes have been applied.

paragraphs.name: 3400-SEND-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph renders the account update screen to the bank operator's terminal, displaying all current account and customer data (including any validation error highlights) so the operator can review, correct, or confirm the information before submitting changes.

paragraphs.name: 3400-SEND-SCREEN-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal termination point for the screen-sending routine, marking the end of the process that displays the account update screen to the bank operator. It is a structural boundary paragraph that allows the program to cleanly exit the screen display logic and return control to the calling section.

paragraphs.name: 9000-READ-ACCT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph orchestrates the full retrieval of an existing credit card account record and its associated customer profile, assembling all current data needed to pre-populate the account update screen for bank staff. It sequentially validates the account's existence through the card cross-reference, fetches the financial account details, retrieves the linked customer demographics, and stores everything as the baseline 'before' snapshot against which any operator changes will be compared.

paragraphs.name: 9000-READ-ACCT-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the account reading routine, providing a structured termination marker that allows other parts of the program to branch here cleanly after account retrieval processing is complete.

paragraphs.name: 9200-GETCARDXREF-BYACCT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph looks up the credit card and customer identifiers associated with a given account number by querying the card cross-reference file. It links the account being updated to its corresponding customer profile and card number, or flags a validation error if no matching record exists.

paragraphs.name: 9200-GETCARDXREF-BYACCT-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the card cross-reference lookup routine, marking the end of the process that retrieves card details linked to a given account number. It acts as a structured boundary that allows the program to cleanly return control to the calling section after the lookup has completed.

paragraphs.name: 9300-GETACCTDATA-BYACCT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph retrieves the full credit card account record from the account master file using the account number entered by the bank operator. It validates that the account exists and is accessible, flagging any lookup failures as input errors to prevent the update from proceeding.

paragraphs.name: 9300-GETACCTDATA-BYACCT-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the account data retrieval routine, marking the boundary where control returns to the calling process after account lookup has completed.

paragraphs.name: 9400-GETCUSTDATA-BYCUST
paragraphs.description: This paragraph retrieves the customer demographic record from the customer master file using the customer ID associated with the account being updated. It validates that the customer exists and is accessible, flagging any lookup failure as an input error that will block the update from proceeding.

paragraphs.name: 9400-GETCUSTDATA-BYCUST-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the customer data retrieval routine, marking the boundary where control returns to the calling process after customer demographic information has been looked up by customer number.

paragraphs.name: 9500-STORE-FETCHED-DATA
paragraphs.description: This paragraph captures a snapshot of the current account and customer data retrieved from the database, storing it as the 'before image' baseline. This baseline is used later to detect whether the bank operator has actually changed any values, preventing unnecessary database writes and enabling change-detection logic.

paragraphs.name: 9500-STORE-FETCHED-DATA-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as a formal exit point for the routine that captures and stores retrieved account and customer data into the working area. It is a structural placeholder that marks the end of the data-fetching process, allowing the program to return control cleanly to the calling logic.

paragraphs.name: 9600-WRITE-PROCESSING
paragraphs.description: This paragraph performs the actual database write operation for a validated credit card account update, locking both the financial account and customer demographic records, checking for concurrent modifications, assembling the updated data, and persisting both records to the database — rolling back if either write fails.

paragraphs.name: 9600-WRITE-PROCESSING-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the account update write processing routine. It marks the end of the write operation block, allowing control to return cleanly to the calling logic after all database update steps have been completed.

paragraphs.name: 9700-CHECK-CHANGE-IN-REC
paragraphs.description: This paragraph determines whether the bank operator has actually modified any account or customer data before allowing a database write to proceed. It compares every editable field on the update screen against the original values retrieved from the database, and if any difference is detected, flags the transaction as containing real changes and routes processing accordingly.

paragraphs.name: 9700-CHECK-CHANGE-IN-REC-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the change-detection routine that determines whether the operator has actually modified any account or customer data. It also incorporates shared logic for capturing which function key the operator pressed to trigger the update action.

paragraphs.name: ABEND-ROUTINE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph handles unrecoverable system failures during the account update process. It ensures that when a fatal error occurs, a meaningful diagnostic message is recorded, the error is surfaced to operations staff, and the transaction is formally terminated with a recognisable failure code so that support teams can identify and investigate the incident.

paragraphs.name: ABEND-ROUTINE-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point of the abnormal-termination handling routine, cleanly concluding the error recovery process. It also incorporates shared date formatting utilities used throughout the account update transaction.
